Natalie Harp, one of President Donald Trump’s closest aides, is reportedly leaning into her nickname “the human printer” by passing along messages to the president the best way she knows how: printing them out.

Harp, 35, is known to carry a portable printer to present physical copies of supportive social media posts or op-eds for Trump to review, because it’s the president’s preferred method of digesting content.

But she also does the same for messages, according to a Politico article.

One person who wanted to give a physical message to Trump told Politico they texted the material to Harp, who replied, “printed.”

The one-word response is apparently the closest someone can get to a read receipt from the president.

open image in gallery Natalie Harp is one of President Trump’s most devoted aides and is constantly seen at his side, providing him with physical copies of flattering op-eds or social media posts to keep his spirits high ( AFP/Getty )

White House Spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement, “Natalie Harp is one of the most loyal and hardest working aides on President Trump's team.”

Harp has been a loyal aide to Trump for many years. She’s consistently photographed at the president’s side or, at least, nearby – sometimes holding a stack of papers for Trump to review.

One of her main duties is to provide Trump with a stream of positive news, op-eds and social media commentary while also showing him criticisms of his opponents. After compiling the content, she prints it out for the president to physically see.

Some of that content, once physically approved by the president, ends up on his Truth Social account, the Wall Street Journal reported.

But Harp also serves as the go-between for the president and allies, facilitating messages for Trump to see and respond to.

open image in gallery Harp’s nickname ‘the human printer’ stems from her job to print out physical copies of social media posts, articles, op-eds and messages for President Trump to review. One New York Times report alleged Harp carried a portable printer around to do so at any given time ( Reuters )

By establishing herself as the source of Trump’s positive feedback and casual communications, Harp has cemented herself as a crucial part of the Trump team in the White House. She’s so devoted to the president that she’s written heartfelt letters saying “You are all that matters to me,” the New York Times reported.

Trump seemingly returns the feelings, treating Harp as a “Binkie” or “his comfort blanket,” New York Times reporter Maggie Haberman described on MSNOW.

Harp’s unwavering allegiance to Trump has sparked speculation about the two’s close-knit relationship.

Harp’s brother, Preston Harp, described the relationship between the president and his sister as “very unhealthy” in an interview with The Daily Mail.

open image in gallery Harp is consistently at the president’s side and has been for many years, cementing her place in Trump’s inner circle ( AFP/Getty )

Preston Harp later told The Daily Beast that he believes his sister sees Trump “as a kind of father figure because he embodies the doctrine of American exceptionalism.”

This past month, Harp was among the few aides that Trump took with him on a military jet when he discreetly changed planes while flying out of Turkey due to security concerns.

Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff used the report to criticize the president, claiming he would rather “travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace” than do his job.

On behalf of the White House, Ingle said: “Jon Ossoff is a cringeworthy, feminine theatre kid cosplaying as Barack Obama. Nobody gives a s*** what this lightweight loser says.”

Netflix is looking to cast people who have undergone a major body transformation for its new reality dating series, Weight to Date.

The streamer announced Tuesday that the unscripted dating show will follow singles “during and after extreme weight loss as they navigate dating, identity, and the search for lasting love.”

Included in the press release is a link to the website www.WeightToDateCasting.com to apply for the debut season. At the top of the form is the question, “Are you ready to find love after a significant body change?”

It adds: “This new inspiring dating series will highlight the journeys of selected singles who are discovering what dating is like after a major body transformation.”

Applicants must be at least 18 years old and a legal U.S. resident.

open image in gallery New Netflix dating series, 'Weight to Date,' will feature singles who have undergone a major body transformation ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery Streamer put out an open casting call for people to apply to be on the debut season ( AFP/Getty )

According to Deadline, the series will follow more of a documentary format, focusing on 10 to 12 people, some of whom have lost a drastic amount of weight and are ready to enter the dating scene.

Weight to Date is just Netflix’s latest unscripted dating series, following Age of Attraction, which mixed 40 singles between the ages of 22 and 60. Its portfolio also includes Love is Blind, where singles date through a wall and get engaged sight-unseen,Temptation Island and the seven-time Emmy-winning reality show Love on the Spectrum.

A premiere date for Weight to Date has not yet been announced.

The show arrives at a time when weight-loss drugs, specifically GLP-1 injectables Ozempic and Wegovy, are surging in popularity in the U.S.

Data collected by Gallup found that GLP-1 usage has nearly quadrupled since 2024, up from 3 percent to 11 percent in 2026.

open image in gallery GLP-1 drug usage in the U.S. has surged in recent years ( PA )

Ozempic was first approved by the FDA in 2017 as a treatment for type 2 diabetes. In 2021, it became a top choice among celebrities and influencers to curb appetites and therefore shed weight.

That same year, the maker of Ozempic launched Wegovy, an FDA-approved solution to help with chronic weight management.

Several famous faces, including tennis superstar Serena Williams and This Is Us actor Chrissy Metz, have opened up about their use of GLP-1 drugs. Both Williams and Metz have even signed on with Ro, a telehealth company, as ambassadors to promote its weight-loss medications and platform.

“I’m not getting any younger,” Metz told People in August of her decision to start taking a GLP-1. “I’m in perimenopause, and there were obesity issues within my family and with my father, and I felt like I’ve tried so many modalities, whether it was diets or therapy, and none of it really worked for me.”

The Government should prioritise cheap energy over decarbonising Britain’s power grid, senior Conservative Claire Coutinho will say.

The shadow energy secretary will lay out her party’s case for planning to ditch net zero in a speech on Wednesday.

Ms Coutinho will insist the UK “should focus all our attention on making electricity cheap, and then let consumer choice be king”.

Reaching net zero by 2050, the policy aimed at balancing out the amount of greenhouse gases with those being removed from the atmosphere, was introduced by the Conservative government under Theresa May in 2019.

Ed Miliband continued the drive towards net zero as energy secretary, followed by Miatta Fahnbulleh, since Labour came into power – and the party is aiming to make the grid 95% carbon-free by 2030.

But Kemi Badenoch has declared the 2050 target is impossible to meet.

The Tory leader has vowed to scrap the policy, and is blocking Conservatives who support net zero from standing as parliamentary candidates in the next general election.

The Conservatives have commissioned Tory-leaning think tank Onward and advisory firm Transira Energy to compare the costs of a net zero electricity grid with one which prioritises cheap power through a mix of gas, more nuclear and fewer renewables.

The analysis by Onward suggested focusing on cheap power could save families £540 a year from their energy bills.

In her speech, Ms Coutinho is expected to say: “Ed Miliband’s Clean Power 2030 target is intent on squeezing every last drop of carbon out of our electricity no matter the cost.

“But making electricity expensive puts electrification out of reach for ordinary families, and it’s moving our industry to more polluting countries overseas – forcing us to import back those same goods with higher emissions.

“That is not improving the climate. It is madness – especially when electrification is a far bigger prize than perfectly clean electricity when it comes to reducing emissions.”

She will add: “Rather than forcing people to do what we want, our job as politicians should be to lift the barriers in their way. That’s why we should focus all our attention on making electricity cheap, and then let consumer choice be king.

“That is the only approach that will work in the long term.

“That’s why for the economy or for the environment, cheap electricity is the holy grail.”

Ahead of the speech, Conservative leader Mrs Badenoch said: “Britain needs a serious plan to deal with climate change. Seriousness means looking at results, not simply setting targets and congratulating ourselves afterwards.

“Current Net Zero targets have driven up energy costs, weakened our industrial base, and made us more dependent on energy imports, while doing too little to make the country more resilient to floods, droughts, and other consequences of the changing climate.

“This report shows what a common sense approach looks like. Unlike Labour, who are wedded to the old failing plans; or Reform, who still don’t believe climate change is happening, the Conservatives will protect our environment, protect our energy security and make energy cheaper. Our plan means using our own oil and gas in the North Sea, removing unnecessary costs from energy bills, and backing cheap, reliable, abundant energy for homes and businesses.”

Labour accused the Tories of “following Reform’s lead” in their policy direction on oil and gas, which they said would “tie Britain to the fossil fuel rollercoaster and keep bills higher for families.”

Energy Secretary Ms Fahnbulleh said: “Labour is investing in more clean energy jobs, cutting tax on electricity bills to give families breathing space this winter and we’re taking action to tackle the climate crisis and bring down bills for good. Kemi Badenoch would put jobs at risk and increase bills.

“As global fossil fuel prices continue to rise amid conflict overseas and wildfires rage across the UK, we can’t turn our back on clean power. That won’t bring down bills and it won’t address the climate crisis. The Tories don’t have a clue.”

The lone Democratic member on the Federal Communications Commission praised Disney and ABC Tuesday for suing to stop the Trump administration from reviewing its broadcasting license ahead of schedule, accusing her boss of trying to bend the law.

Anna Gomez, a commissioner on the FCC, said in a statement she was “glad Disney has shown courage and stepped up” to challenge President Donald Trump’s attempts to exert more control over broadcasts by threatening to revoke licenses.

“It is time this administration understands that the Constitution does not bend to political convenience, and that the First Amendment protects the news and commentary Americans see on their screens even when those in power wish it didn’t,” Gomez wrote.

Her bold statement came shortly after Disney and ABC sued the FCC for trying to force a review of its broadcast licenses years before they expire. The media companies allege the effort is part of an ongoing censorship campaign, citing Trump’s critical statements about ABC.

Gomez has previously issued statements in opposition to Trump and FCC Commissioner Brendan Carr’s ongoing pressure campaign against ABC.

open image in gallery FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez, the only Democrat on the commission, was openly supportive of Disney and ABC’s lawsuit against the FCC, accusing the Trump administration of trying to skirt the First Amendment ( Getty )

She’s previously accused her bosses of “targeting Disney” in a “campaign of censorship and control” because the administration has been highly critical of ABC’s reporting and shows such as “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” and “The View.”

Gomez reiterated her concerns Tuesday, saying the FCC’s decision to threaten Disney’s ABC stations with broadcast license revocations was motivated by a desire “to punish a company for speech this administration doesn’t like.”

Earlier this year, the FCC ordered eight Disney-owned television stations to file broadcast license renewals at least two years ahead of schedule.

The request came after months of pressure from the administration and highly critical comments from Trump.

Already, the FCC had launched an investigation into Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion practices as well as a separate probe into “The View” — a show that Trump has called “pathetic.”

The commission had also been embroiled in a controversy with late-night show “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” after Kimmel made critical remarks following Charlie Kirk’s death. Carr threatened to revoke ABC stations’ broadcast licenses, causing the stations to pull Kimmel’s show temporarily from the air.

open image in gallery Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel has been part of the ongoing feud between ABC and President Trump after several broadcast stations pulled Kimmel’s show ( Getty )

But long before the incident, Trump had called Kimmel “stupid,” untalented, and said he hoped to play a “major part” in forcing the late-night host, among others, off the air.

Disney and ABC cited these instances of alleged “retaliation” in its lawsuit, saying it amounted to coercion to comply with Trump’s preferences.

Disney is asking a federal judge in Washington, D.C., to stop the FCC from taking or threatening to take action against the company and its ABC stations related to early license renewal applications.

Several people, including Gomez, have backed Disney and ABC’s efforts, including the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, which called the suit “the day of reckoning for Brendan Carr,” and Senator Bernie Sanders, who described it as pushback against a “dictatorship.”

Gomez said the lawsuit “should be a welcome sign for every broadcaster who has felt the weight of this overreaching government pressure in silence.”

A Georgia man burglarized former NASCAR driver Greg Biffle's home after learning Biffle and his family died in a plane crash, a North Carolina sheriff said Tuesday.

Terrell Williams, 44, has been charged with second-degree burglary, safe cracking, money laundering and other felonies, Iredell County Sheriff Darren Campbell announced at a news conference. Williams was being held without bond in Cobb County, Georgia, on suspicion of another home burglary. Jail records did not list an attorney.

Campbell said investigators were led to Williams in July, when Cobb County police arrested him and found items taken from Biffle's home.

Biffle, his wife and his two children, along with three others, died in the Dec. 18 crash, which remains under investigation by the NTSB.

Authorities reported a break-in at the home on Jan. 8 and have said $30,000 in cash, two Glock handguns, NASCAR memorabilia and gold and silver coins were stolen.

Investigators have recovered some of the stolen items, including NASCAR memorabilia, Campbell said. They also found a radio-frequency detector they believe Williams used during the burglary to locate security cameras.

He said Williams is also suspected in another North Carolina burglary that occurred when a law enforcement officer was in the hospital.

“He used headlines, social media posts, different things to find out when people were and were not home, and he executed his plan in that capacity,” Campbell said.

Campbell said investigators have also identified a person of interest in a separate fraud case following the Biffle family's death.

Investigators have said bank, Venmo and PayPal accounts tied to the Biffles were accessed online using personal information, with phone numbers and email addresses changed to gain control of funds. Money was then allegedly transferred to accounts not belonging to the family and used for purchases, according to a search warrant affidavit.

At least one fraudulent check tied to Biffle’s business interests was cashed, and other attempts were made to access accounts. The activity occurred across multiple states.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: five new signings to consider

Tarik Muharemović (£2.7m)

News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: five key budget enablers
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.

Telegraph Fantasy Football managers need to make compromises to fit in fantasy heavyweights like Erling Haaland (£8.3m) and Bruno Fernandes (6.5m). Picking some set-and-forget budget enablers who have either high point ceiling potential or will return a steady stream of points, is key to freeing up those funds.

Below are five players the Fantasy Football Hub experts have highlighted for consideration.





Brian Brobbey (£3.3m)

The Sunderland forward had a steady Premier League debut season, netting seven times and helping the Black Cats qualify for the Europa League. The Dutch international netted three times at the World Cup, improving his stock further, and will be looking to get off to a goal-scoring start against Ipswich and Fulham in GWs 1 and 2.



Enzo Le Fee (£3.3m)

Depending on the formation TFF managers are using, Brobbey’s midfield teammate at the same price may be the preferred route to target those opening fixtures. The 26-year-old accrued 12 attacking returns last season, and bumped up his overall score with an impressive 93 tackles.



Harry Wilson (£3.2m)

The midfielder swapped London for Yorkshire in the summer, as he looks to expand on a whopping 17 attacking returns from last season. Feeding the rejuvenated Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£3.9m), and adding goals from midfield for Leeds will be two primary objectives for the Welsh international, who could make a mockery of his mere marginal price increase.



James Trafford (£3.0m)

Another Leeds United summer acquisition, Daniel Farke fought off rival Premier League suitors to land the ex-Manchester City shot-stopper. Leeds United have a mixed bag in terms of opening fixture difficulty, but do have three home league games in the first five before the international break, and the new no.1 has an outside chance of getting the nod in the Carabao Cup games too, so there are points available should the Whites be able to shut out the opposition.



James Hill (£2.6m)

If looking to fit in more big-hitters, a sub £3m player can be extremely useful for team balance, and the Bournemouth defender looks assured of starting having played a pivotal role in getting the Cherries into Europe this season.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: five essential players for the 2026/27 season
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub, will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount.

Five best fantasy football players





Take a look at these elite Telegraph Fantasy Football tips below:



Erling Haaland (£8.3m)

Comfortably last season’s top points scorer with 254, the Norwegian striker will once again likely be the first name in TFF Managers’ XIs. Having come back late from his post-World Cup break, there may be nervousness about early-season minutes. However, if he keeps up his phenomenal August goals-to-games ratio, starting without him may mean playing catch-up against the field.



João Pedro (£5.1m)

Having missed out on the Brazilian squad for the World Cup, the forward looks rejuvenated after a rested summer, netting seven times and assisting twice more in pre-season. With no European distractions for the Blues this season, and attacking intent shown in new manager Xabi Alonso’s selections thus far, the 24-year-old looks primed for a successful season.



Antoine Semenyo (£4.9m)

Perhaps one of the biggest surprises in the pricing for the new season was the City winger’s sub-£5m tag. The January recruit was the second-highest scorer in the game last season, and has looked the most dangerous of Enzo Moresca’s attacking assets in pre-season, so looks the stand-out midfield option.



Gabriel Magalhães (£4.9m)

Another that perhaps warranted a higher price increase, the Brazilian only missed out on breaking the 200-point barrier due to his injury late in the season. While there are cheaper options in the champions’ backline, including Christhian Mosquera (£3.7m), who looks likely to deputise for the injured William Saliba (£4.6m), getting the assurances over long-term starts and the additional attacking returns is enough to warrant paying the higher expense.



Nico O’Reilly (£4.2m)

The England international has incurred a position change in TFF, and will now gain points for clean sheets as a defender on top of his attacking returns. Had he scored as a defender last season, he would have topped his position table; therefore, £4.2m seems too good value to turn down.



One notable omission from the list is Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m). It isn’t through the belief that the veteran won’t return heavily once again this season, but rather that there appears to be more value across a wide range of mid-priced options where TFF managers can optimise value across their starting XIs.

News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Sports.title: Dead body found at Charlton Athletic's stadium as police launch investigation
Sports.content:
Dead body found at Charlton Athletic's stadium as police launch investigation

Charlton Athletic have announced they are assisting police with an investigation after a deceased individual was discovered at their stadium on Tuesday morning

View 2 Images Charlton released a statement on Tuesday evening (Image: Getty Images)

A dead body has been found at Charlton Athletic's stadium, The Valley. A statement from the Addicks on Tuesday night confirmed a deceased individual had been discovered earlier that day.

‌



Charlton say they are assisting police with their enquiries after the incident which is said to have occurred in the early hours of Monday morning. A male was pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



The club stress there is no suggestion of any wrongdoing on their part.

‌



The statement read: "Charlton Athletic are supporting the police with their enquiries following the discovery of a deceased individual at The Valley on Tuesday morning.

"Police were called to the stadium today after an incident that occurred in the early hours of Monday morning. A male was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

Sports.title: Premier League chief makes Man City 115 charges admission as case drags on
Sports.content:
Premier League chief makes Man City 115 charges admission as case drags on

Manchester City remain under the microscope following over 100 alleged breaches of the Premier League’s spending rules and Richard Masters has offered a fresh update

View 2 Images Premier League chief Richard Masters (Image: Getty Images)

The ruling into Manchester City’s 115 breaches of spending rules is ‘taking longer than expected’, Premier League CEO Richard Masters has admitted. City were charged with more than 100 breaches of the division’s financial rules following a lengthy investigation.

‌



As yet, an independent commission is yet to publish a ruling, more than 18 months after a disciplinary hearing came to an end. From their end, City have also maintained their innocence.

‌



Speaking to the BBC, Masters admitted that the process has taken longer than first thought, but has underlined that certain rules have to be followed in such cases.

‌



"I do accept it's taking longer than expected, and I understand that people want to find out as soon as possible what's going on, but I simply can't provide that," Masters said.

"Our rules are very clear - we have to follow the process, and there's only one real clear route through, which is to allow that process to reach its natural conclusion."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



City are not the only Premier League side to have been charged for breaches of Premier League rules. Everton, Nottingham Forest and Leicester City have all fallen foul of Profit and Sustainability rules over recent seasons and faced points deductions.

Meanwhile, Chelsea were fined £10m and given a suspended transfer ban for breaching rules relating to payments to agents. A points deduction was also dealt out, albeit was cancelled upon appeal.

Explaining the difference between the Man City and Chelsea cases, Masters said: "In the situation with Chelsea, obviously it's historic. It's very different to PSR cases. In the case of Chelsea, the new owners came forward with all the information, and we decided to enter a sanction agreement.

‌



"That sanction agreement was was overseen by a commission as well, and part of the role of the commission is to assure that that sanction is not unduly lenient.

View 2 Images City are still waiting on a verdict on their 115 charges

"I think the key difference is, given the evidence base and given the lack of witnesses, none of the people involved with these payments are still at the club, we not able to interview them, the evidence base isn't complete.

‌



"The alternative to entering the sanction agreement was to go down a contested commission route. I'm not sure we'd have been able to bring all of the charges that the club ultimately admitted to, or be successful in getting them, so I don't think there was an easy choice for the board to make.

"We took a decision that the sanction agreement was the best thing for the league, and we're fully aware that not everyone agrees that that was the right course of action, and we just have to accept that."

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney insists Marcus Rashford can break his Man Utd goal record in 'second chance'
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney insists Marcus Rashford can break his Man Utd goal record in 'second chance'

Marcus Rashford is set to return to Manchester United this summer following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona and Wayne Rooney has issued some strong instructions to the forward

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has returned to Man United following a loan spell with Barcelona (Image: Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney believes Marcus Rashford could break his Manchester United goalscoring record but only if he knuckles down at Old Trafford. The Red Devils forward is set to return to United this summer following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona.

‌



The Spanish side had the option to sign him permanently, but chose not, that decision leaving Rashford in the uncomfortable position of attempting to relaunch his United career 18 months after his last appearance.

‌



Despite that, Rooney still believes he could surpass his long-standing club record of 253 goals, but only if he works harder. Rashford currently has 138 goals to his name for the club and sits 15th in their all-time top scorers list.

‌



Speaking on the Rest is United, Rooney said: “I think his work rate has to improve. But if he wants to be at the football club, he just needs to knuckle down.

“He’s a young lad, he’s from Manchester… he’s the one player who can go and get my goalscoring record.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“I don’t want want to see Marcus Rashford doing well at Aston Villa or doing well at Barcelona, I want to see him doing well at Man Utd and scoring goals for Man Utd.

“But that means he just needs to get his head down, work his socks off and be more positive, play with a smile on his face.

“When he gets the ball – it happened a few times the other day where he gets the ball and stands the defenders up and just knocks it back inside.

‌



“This is what I said to him a couple of years ago – when you get the ball and you’ve got a full-back one-v-one, touch, knock it past them and run.

View 2 Images Rooney has offered former teammate Marcus Rashford some advice (Image: Getty Images)

“You don’t have to do stepovers, you don’t have to slow it down because the best thing the defender can do is put a slide tackle in because it’s very rare that one of the full-backs is as quick as you. You might get a corner or throw-in, you might get a free kick in a dangerous area, you might win a penalty.

‌



“Be positive, it gets the crowd up, it gets the fans singing, they’re behind you. And that’s what the fans want to see – entertaining players, being positive.”

Rashford has continued to be linked with moves away from United this summer but Rooney has urged him to stay and thrive under Michael Carrick.

He added: “He’s got a manager who he’s played with, he knows, he respects. He’s from Manchester, he’s a Man Utd fan.

‌



“He’s got the opportunity to restart his Man Utd career. It is crazy that he would want to go anywhere else. Absolutely crazy.

“He’s not that far away from my goalscoring record, so whatever has happened before with previous managers, the club, whatever, he has to just say, ‘I’m a very lucky lad, I’ve got the opportunity to still be here at Man Utd and actually start again.’

“It’s on him, nobody else. He’s got nobody left to blame. He has to take responsibility because if not, the fans will turn on him very quick.”

Sports.title: Barcelona star Gavi responds to Man Utd transfer interest as Red Devils eye THIRD midfielder
Sports.content:
Barcelona star Gavi responds to Man Utd transfer interest as Red Devils eye THIRD midfielder

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick remains keen on adding to his midfield options despite the signings of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos with Barcelona's Gavi now a target

View 2 Images The Red Devils had plotted a deal for Gavi (Image: Getty Images)

Spanish World Cup winner Gavi has snubbed a move to Manchester United.

‌



United boss Michael Carrick had targeted the 22-year-old in a bid to bolster his midfield options ahead of the new season. It's understood United were willing to meet Barcelona's £35m asking price.

‌



But Gavi has made it clear he wants to remain with the Spanish champions - and has no interest in joining United. The news will come as a blow to United fans, who have become frustrated with United's lack of serious transfer business this summer.

‌



While some of their rivals have spent big on new signings, United have spent a combined £85m on Youri Tielemans and Chelsea reject Andrey Santos.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Gavi signed for Barca at the age of 11 and has gone on to make 119 league appearances since making his debut in 2021. He missed five months of last season due to a serious knee injury.

‌



But regained his form and fitness in March to earn a place in the Spain squad for this summer's World Cup.

He made two appearances during the tournament, and was an unused substitute in the final which saw Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in New York.

He is under contract at the Nou Camp until 2030, where boss Hansi Flick is reluctant to let him leave. Speaking about his relationship with the Barcelona boss at the end of last season, Gavi said: "I have suffered a lot, unfortunately, in these last two years. It's football.

‌



View 2 Images Carrick is still keen on adding to his midfield options (Image: Getty Images)

"They were serious injuries and you have to be mentally strong, and I have been. It's a strong point of mine. I'm at this level because of the mentality I have. It is not easy to play at this pace, coming from two serious injuries. I've done it and I'm proud.

"Luckily, the coach trusts me a lot. He's like a father to me. I am very grateful to him. It's not easy to get to play after this injury. He knows about my talent and mentality and that it's important for the team. He blindly trusts me."

Article continues below

Gavi’s desire to stay in Spain will force United to look elsewhere in Carrick’s bid to sign a third midfielder this summer, albeit the clock is now ticking.

Away from their midfield, United's only other business saw them move for goalkeeper Karl Darlow on a free transfer. The Red Devils have also said farewell to a number of stars including Rasums Hojlund and Casemiro, while goalkeepers Radek Vitek and Altay Bayindir have both departed.

Sports.title: Harry Kane's stance on mega-money transfer as England captain targeted in Bayern swoop
Sports.content:
Harry Kane's stance on mega-money transfer as England captain targeted in Bayern swoop

Former Tottenham Hotspur striker Harry Kane has been linked with a move away from Bayern Munich with a Saudi Pro League club keen on the England captain

View 2 Images England captain Harry Kane has been linked with a move away from Bayern Munich (Image: Leonhard Simon/Getty Images)

Harry Kane is being targeted by Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, with the former Tottenham Hotspur striker’s future at Bayern Munich under the microscope. The England captain is currently preparing for his fourth season at Bayern , having left Spurs back in 2023.

‌



Kane has returned to Bayern after being granted an extended summer break following his involvement with the England squad at the World Cup, and has now entered the final 12 months of his contract with the Bundesliga champions. As a result, there have been rumours about whether or not the 33-year-old will put pen to paper on an extension, or leave the Allianz Arena to join a new club.

‌



Saudi billionaires Al Hilal are plotting a sensational swoop for Kane. But Kane is not prepared to join the Saudi Pro League at this stage of his career - and is closing in on a new deal with Bayern.

‌



8 blockbuster deals that could be completed in final two weeks of the transfer window READ MORE :

Wayne Rooney demands four Man Utd signings and tells Marcus Rashford to buck up ideas READ MORE :

Kane tops Hilal's shortlist of future signings, which also includes Ollie Watkins and Victor Osimhen. And Hilal president Nawaf bin Saad will keep tabs on Kane's situation, with a view to luring him to Saudi in the future with a deal worth a whopping £1.2m-a-week.

Kane has entered the final 12 months of his current deal with Bayern, and wants to extend it. The former Tottenham striker put talks on hold until after the World Cup, where he led England to within minutes of a place in the final.

‌



View 2 Images Harry Kane captained England in this summer's World Cup. (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

With rumours around Kane’s future continuing to generate speculation, the striker recently addressed his contract situation at Bayern, where he admitted that he is “relaxed” about his future.

“We obviously said we wanted to talk after the World Cup and after my holiday,” Kane said last month, via Kicker. “So I’m not sure exactly when, but they’ll start this week, next week… we’ll start those talks.

‌



“Like I’ve said before, we’re calm, I think they’re calm with the situation.

“Obviously now is the time to start talking, because there’s only a year left. That’s important. But both sides are relaxed, and I’m pretty sure there’ll be some talks this week or next week.”

Sports.title: Chelsea change name of under-21s side in controversial move to rebrand academy
Sports.content:
Chelsea change name of under-21s side in controversial move to rebrand academy

Chelsea's owners have released a statement to explain the decision to change the name of their under-21 and under-19s sides to Cobham Next Gen (CNG), much to the annoyance of fans

View 2 Images Chelsea's under-21s and under-19s sides have been renamed (Image: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Chelsea have angered their fanbase by deciding to rename their under-19 and under-21s sides. From now on, the club will refer to them as Cobham Next Gen (CNG).

‌



Chelsea have one of the most famous and prolific academies in English football, having helped develop a vast array of talented players. It seems that, under the ownership of BlueCo, the club now want to establish a separate brand for their academy, which is based in Cobham, Surrey.

‌



The Blues claim that Cobham Next Gen "accurately reflects the age profile" of the players in the academy sides and strengthens its identity.

‌



"The new name more accurately reflects the age profile of our leading academy side and Chelsea's long-standing heritage of developing the next generation of players for the senior game," the club said in a statement.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Cobham Next Gen also better fits the role of the squad within the academy. It recognises a group of young players with momentum, taking the next step in their development - the final one in the pathway to senior football - competing at a higher level as they continue their journey through Cobham towards the men's team."

‌



It added: "The introduction of Cobham Next Gen also strengthens the academy's identity. More than an age-group name, it represents the players progressing through Cobham and the opportunities available to them as they continue their development towards the men's game.

"This new identity reflects the distinction of Chelsea’s academy as a unique footballing environment with its own history, culture and proven record of developing players for the highest level of the game."

View 2 Images Chelsea's under-21s won the Premier League 2 title last season (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



The move has not gone down well on social media. "Sounds like an eSports team," one fan responded. "Okay so what is the reason for this actually?" another added.

A third wrote: "BlueCo have massively underestimated the UK-wide anti-sentiment of the franchising/americanisation of our game." "We are legitimately going to be called the London Cowboys in 2 years," predicted another fan.

Another simply wrote: "This is a really poor and crazy decision. The Club is CHELSEA Football Club."

‌



Cobham Next Gen will be lead by head coach Harry Hudson in the upcoming 2026/27 season. Hudson was promoted to lead the under-21s last season after Calum McFarlane was elevated to the first team to become interim manager in between the spells of Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior. Chelsea's under-21s won the Premier League 2 last season, winning 14 of their 20 matches.

The decision comes the day after it emerged that Chelsea shareholders Todd Boehly and Mark Walter are in talks to to sell their stakes in the Premier League club to majority owner Clearlake Capital. The BlueCo consortium including Boehly, Walter and Clearlake purchased Chelsea in a deal worth £2.5billion four years ago.

A report from The Financial Times claims that Boehly, Chelsea's chairman and co-controlling owner, and board member Walter have been in discussions to sell their respective 12.8 per cent stakes. The deal would value the club at more than £5bn.

Sports.title: Man Utd forced into kit change before season has started to avoid rule break
Sports.content:
Man Utd forced into kit change before season has started to avoid rule break

Manchester United have had to make a change to one of their new kits already this summer

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes in the new Manchester United third kit (Image: 2026 Eurasia Sport Images)

Manchester United have been forced to make a change to one of their kits before the season has even kicked off in order to avoid breaking UEFA rules. The club’s new third strip was released last week.

‌



It features three eye-catching central logos: the Red Devil crest, a Snapdragon fireball emblem and an Adidas' three-stripe logo. It marks a rapid departure from the club's home and away kits this season, as it doesn't feature 'Snapdragon' written across the front of the shirt.

‌



The Old Trafford outfit have explained that they will have to alter the shirt for the Champions League, however. This means United's third shirt in Europe will feature the Snapdragon word mark, the same as their home and away strip, and not the Snapdragon symbol.

‌



UEFA insist that jerseys worn in the Champions League must all be consistent with one another, meaning United's third kit must stay consistent their home and away.

A club statement read: "You have probably noticed that there is a different look to the latter, too. Our new third shirt doesn't feature the traditional 'Snapdragon' wordmark, yet the sponsor is still recognisable through its fireball, which has been ever-present on United's jerseys since the start of the 2024/25 campaign.

Man Utd holding Bruno Fernandes future talks after big money offer received READ MORE :

"On our latest release, it forms part of an aesthetic three-pronged design down the centre of the shirt, done in agreement with adidas and Snapdragon to provide the jersey with a fresh style and clean look that is unique for this season.

‌



"The Reds are due to sport the jersey when required across domestic competition this term, although UEFA rules mean that the 'Snapdragon' wordmark will be added to our players' shirts for any Champions League matches it is worn in.

"This is because the same version of a logo must be used across all of a club's kits in the tournament, so the sponsor on the third strip needs to match that on our new home and away releases, which feature the wordmark."

View 3 Images United's third shirt will have to align with the club's home shirt in the Champions League (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



Snapdragon have been the club's primary sponsor since the beginning of the 2024/25 season. Sportswear giant Adidas signed a 10-year deal with United in 2023 worth a staggering £900million.

Michael Carrick‘s side will kick off their Premier League season with an away trip to newly-promoted Hull on Saturday. They end the summer having suffered two defeats in pre-season against Wrexham and Milan, but they secured wins against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid, and drew against Paris Saint-Germain and Leeds.

"I think, as a whole, it's been good," Carrick told MUTV. "I think there are a lot of positives to take from it. I think a lot of the performances, I think the group has grown and got stronger.

‌



View 3 Images United's third kit will look slightly different in the Champions League (Image: © 2026 SOPA Images)

"But on the whole, we're ready for next week. I think a lot of the boys will be better for the minutes, and as I said, we've done a lot of work on the training pitch. I think the performances in the games have been pretty good, so we're still in good spirits going into next week."

‌



United are also back amongst Europe’s elite for the first time in three years. They will find out their Champions League fate when the fixture list for the league phase is drawn on August 26.

The club will be in pot two. United will play eight league games, four at home and four away, but will not face another Premier League side.

Sports.title: Man Utd are sleepwalking into Bruno Fernandes transfer issue - the harsh truth is clear
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is known to loving supporters by his first name.

But those chants of “Bruno” which ring around Old Trafford and beyond, fail to reflect what he has contributed to the club since joining them.

Perhaps calling him the 'Coal Man' might be more fitting tribute. Due to the huge weight he has carried on his back in recent times.

Forget him being 'Player of the Year' more times than some people can remember. Fernandes has been United's player of the last decade - and he hasn't even been at Old Trafford that long!

‌



United's transfer business in this period has been shambolic. But Fernandes has bucked the status quo - and then some. The Portuguese has been one of the few shining lights in a period of almost terminal decline at one of the world's supposed biggest clubs.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Before signing Fernandes from Sporting Lisbon in 2020, United's recruitment team held a meeting in a room at the club's Carrington training complex. One senior member showed a video of Fernandes kicking a dressing room door in, after being shown a red card.

‌



That person questioned whether the midfielder had the temperament to deal with the pressure and expectation that comes with being a United footballer. Until the then chief executive Ed Woodward stepped into the debate, insisting he loved the passion and desire Fernandes had shown.

A few weeks later a United delegation flew to Lisbon to seal a £47m deal. Which has gone on to resemble chicken feed, considering the fees some footballers are now commanding in today's inflated market.

View 3 Images Fernandes is coming off, arguably, the best season of his Manchester United career (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

In recent weeks United have found themselves fending off interest in Fernandes from numerous clubs at home and abroad. It was the same last summer, when three from Saudi's Pro League came calling.

‌



'Groundhog Day' has become part of Fernandes's life at United.

It's understood Fernandes informed club bosses a few weeks ago he had no intention of leaving. A new and improved deal will be winging its way to Fernandes and his representatives.

But since committing himself to United, verbally at least, the intervening weeks have seen co-owners the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe do little to make their star attraction feel like he's made the right decision.

View 3 Images United have been unable to match their captain's upward trajectory (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



While the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea and even Tottenham have spent big on strengthening their squad, United have failed to provide Fernandes with help when it comes to sharing the burden of getting winning results this season.

Which begs the question, how long will it be before Fernandes gets tired of being the talisman of a side which has no realistic chance of winning the title?

Getting into the Champions League is now deemed a successful season. That's how far the standards have dropped at United.

The harsh truth is that someone like Fernandes deserves better. And it's only a matter of time before he realises this.

‌



And if and when this happens, the finger of blame will be pointing straight at the Glazers and Ratcliffe.

Sports.title: Arteta: We want to be the best club in the world
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta is excited to keep building Arsenal after their Premier League win, vowing to make them "the best club in the world".

The Gunners lifted the trophy last season for the first time in 22 years, and have already made moves to bolster their defence of it, with key arrivals such as Christian Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes.

Arteta says they will keep targeting elite players to get Arsenal to the very top.

"It's certainly the ambition of the club and the owners to be the best club in the world," he told Sky Sports at a Premier League launch event ahead of their Friday night opener against Coventry, live on Sky.

"In order to do that, you need the best facilities, the best stadium, the best supporters, and you need the best squad and the best players in the world.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Savundra and Michael Bridge discuss were Arsenal need to strengthen this summer.

"Those are the ones that win you football matches and the ones that can be decisive when it matters.

"That's what we try to build with the actual players that we have, and with the players that we want to sign to make the difference for Arsenal."

Arsenal go into the season as outright favourites to retain their title, with that status further underlined by their comfortable 3-0 win over Manchester City in Sunday's Community Shield.

Arteta, however, says he is more than comfortable with the position of being the frontrunners.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz explains why Arsenal's emphatic win over Manchester City has led to plenty of transfer debates for the Gunners.

"I think this is part of our industry, and that's OK," he said. "For me, it's when I look into the eyes of my players and I see that fire, that desire and the will to be better every single day.

"That's the only thing that I care about."

The weight of history is against Arsenal defending their trophy, however. Arsenal have not defended the top-flight title since the 1990s.

It is another milestone Arteta is keen to overcome.

"That's an opportunity that we have ahead, and we are very conscious of what it's going to take to deliver that," he said.

"But I feel the ambition, I feel the desire, and I feel the ability and the conviction around the team that we can do it."

Arsenal chief: New signings need 'to change the dial'

Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick says the club want to sign players who "are going to change the dial".

The Premier League champions missed out on Vinicius Junior after he signed a new Real Madrid contract, while they are interested in Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez.

Asked about the club being linked with elite players, Garlick said: "It's players that are going to take Arsenal forward.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes during the friendly against Como

"In the past we've looked at players that maybe helped build out the squad or get us to a certain level, but now we're competing right at the top level, and we do need to bring in players that are going to change the dial.

"That might be younger players that come into your squad and give them time to develop, and you've seen that in the last couple of years at Arsenal, and if we're able to combine those players that are coming through the academy with some of the best players in the world then we've got every chance of maintaining that success and going beyond what we've already achieved."

Arsenal have spent £143.5m on four summer signings, including the permanent arrival of defender Piero Hincapie.

Questioned on whether there is still money to be spent, Garlick replied: "We said at the start of this season we're about to embark on that we're not going to stand still and pat ourselves on the back and say, 'Well done, job done, nothing else to do'. We want to move forward - the best clubs are always moving forward.

"You can see we've already invested in the squad this season, and if the right opportunity arises, then we will look to strengthen in all areas.

"The window's open for the next couple of weeks, and if there are players that are going to come in and move Arsenal forward, then we will look at that.

"The standard now is high, though - the bar's been set winning the Premier League title and getting to the Champions League final. We're probably fishing in a smaller pool of quality players, and that means that it's tricky to land those players that are going to drive Arsenal forward.

"But if the right opportunity presents itself, we'll certainly be exploring it."

Analysis: Where could Arsenal strengthen before window shuts?

Arsenal showed why they are considered favourites to retain the Premier League with their dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City, but there is still a possibility that Arteta further reinforces his title-winning squad.

They want to add a forward and a defender. Finding a defender who can soften the blow of William Saliba's extended spell out has led Arsenal to hold talks over potential deals for England internationals Ezri Konsa and Jarell Quansah.

Both players share a similar profile and have the capacity to play at centre-back and right-back, but both look to be difficult deals to do. Aston Villa want £60m for Konsa and there is a big gap in valuation, while Bayer Leverkusen do not currently want to sell Quansah.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara makes his predictions for the new Premier League season, including who he thinks will come out on top as leading goalscorer!

It remains to be seen if Arsenal can achieve their goal of bringing in a statement forward signing after Vinicius Junior chose to stay at Real Madrid. They are interested in Julian Alvarez at Atletico Madrid, while there are also links with Victor Osimhen.

Arsenal had set out to sign a left-winger at the start of the window but will be alert to any opportunities for long-term targets in the final days of the window that could improve the attack in other positions.

Summer signing Christos Tzolis' performance levels have taken many by surprise ahead of the new season, including Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta, which may well convince Arsenal that they have adequately addressed the left-wing position.

Arsenal want to make more from sales this summer in a bid to be more financially sustainable, and they are understood to be willing to listen to offers for Gabriel Martinelli, Ethan Nwaneri and Gabriel Jesus while there is uncertainty around Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Bruno Guimaraes' arrival has raised the prospect of either Lewis-Skelly or Martin Zubimendi departing. However, any deal for Zubimendi would likely require Arsenal to make a return on the £51m they signed him for last summer, while Lewis-Skelly goes down as pure profit.

Sports.title: Venus Williams given US Open wild card - with another held potentially for Serena
Sports.content:
Venus Williams has been given a wild card into the US Open singles draw, and the tournament is keeping one on hold - perhaps in case her sister Serena wants to join her.

Sloane Stephens, the 2017 US Open champion, was one of six other women to receive a wild card, and the US Tennis Association said the final one is still to be announced.

That almost certainly would go to Serena Williams, if she decides she wants to return to the tournament at 44. Coverage of the US Open begins on Sunday August 30, live on Sky Sports Tennis.

Venus received a wild card last year, returning to the tournament she won twice for the first time since 2023.

The 46-year-old became the oldest entrant in singles at the tournament since Renee Richards played at 47 in 1981, according to the International Tennis Federation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Serena and Venus Williams against Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns from the Cincinnati Open

She has continued to play some singles matches and this week joined Serena for their first doubles tournament together since the 2022 US Open. They lost Monday at the Cincinnati Open in a tiebreaker against Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns.

The sisters planned to play at Wimbledon but had to withdraw after Serena injured her knee in her singles match. That marked her first time playing singles since the 2022 US Open, and she indicated afterwards that she hoped to keep competing if healthy.

Image: The last remaining wild card place is understood to have been held back should Serena Williams decide she wants to compete in singles

Headlining the wild card recipients on the men's side were 39-year-old Gael Monfils, set to play his final Grand Slam tournament before retiring, and Australian Alexei Popyrin, who upset Novak Djokovic in 2024 on the way to the fourth round. One spot is also being held among the eight men's wild cards.

The main draw begins on Sunday August 30, with the qualifying tournaments being played earlier that week.

Sports.title: Root won't 'rip up' Bazball blueprint as Babar is ruled out for Pakistan
Sports.content:
Returning England Test skipper Joe Root says he feels "as ready as any other England captain", adding he has no plans on "ripping up" the Bazball blueprint that preceded his second stint in charge.

Root has captained England on a record 65 occasions, his first permanent spell from 2017 to 2022 ending with a run of just one win in 17 Tests before Ben Stokes took over in step with head coach Brendon McCullum.

But, after an impressive first couple of years to the Bazball era, the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer saw Stokes retire from international cricket during the final Test and subsequently prompted McCullum's removal as red-ball head coach.

"I don't think there's a huge amount we need to change. It's small things that will make a big difference," Root said ahead of the three-Test series against Pakistan, which starts on Wednesday at Headingley - live on Sky Sports Cricket, from 10am (first ball 11am).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gives his first interview since being reappointed England Test captain

"It's not about ripping it up, I think it's about keeping a lot of the good stuff we've been doing for a period of time, stuff that Ben and Baz built for a long while.

"I don't believe there is one way of playing Test cricket. You've got to be adaptable and play the situation. It's never the same throughout five days, there's different challenges and you've got to adjust to the ebbs and flows throughout."

As for his own readiness to return to the captaincy, the 35-year-old made it clear he was fully prepared to embrace the challenge one more time.

"The landscape is different," he said. "I'm a different player and person than I was when I [first] took over as captain.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports Cricket podcast, Nasser Hussain fears Joe Root sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes

"I'm in a very fortunate, unique position where I've got 60-odd games of experience to look back on. There are things I might want to change and do slightly differently.

"I had time to step away, play in a different environment, under a different coach, different captain, and see the game from a different lens.

"In many ways I feel as ready as any other England captain that's been before; to have that amount of experience is invaluable."

He added: "I'm really excited. And to get the chance to start at Headingley as well is always nice, my home ground.

"It's a very talented group of players that are very capable of special things. I'm really excited about where we can take this team."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew previously imposed on his team

'Hugely supportive' Brook to remain vice-captain

White-ball skipper Harry Brook, despite serving as Test vice-captain, was overlooked in favour of Root to lead England in Stokes' absence for the second Test against New Zealand at The Oval, as well as for the permanent job upon his international retirement.

Root confirmed Brook will continue in the role as No 2 in the Test team and insisted the pair's bond remains strong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast Nasser Hussain, believes Harry Brook is a 'very good captain' but needs the 'mature Harry to come out' after his England Test captaincy snub

"Our relationship is exactly as it has been for a long time," he said. "Me and Harry are very good friends and get along well away from cricket, and clearly get the best out of each other when playing together.

"He's been hugely supportive. I fully feel like he's got my back, as the rest of the guys do. He's going to be invaluable.

"He's done some brilliant things already within the white-ball space. He's a brilliant leader within the group and the fact he's not captain, that shouldn't be taken away from him."

As for life without Stokes, Root added: "It's a big void to fill. He's someone who has been ever present for the best part of 15 years.

"It's been different, but we've only been together as a full team for a day and a half."

And quizzed on whether he could yet return to the side, with a home Ashes series on the horizon in 2027, Root said: "Who knows? That's a question for Ben.

"We need to look after the here and now, and that's this series."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England managing director Rob Key does not rule out a return to Test cricket for Ben Stokes and why they chose to appoint Joe Root as captain and not Harry Brook

Pakistan captain Babar injured for Headingley

Pakistan captain Babar Azam has been ruled out of the series opener against England due to a finger injury, with Salman Ali Agha taking temporary charge at Headingley.

Image: Pakistan captain Babar Azam will miss the first Test at Headingley due to an injured finger

Babar was initially struck on the right hand when facing the West Indies earlier this month, before he then received another blow from England Under-19 seamer Manny Lumsden in a tour match at Beckenham last week. He retired hurt in what was described at the time as a "precautionary measure".

The tourists were keen to give him time to recover but, while he has been cleared of a broken middle finger, he has not been cleared to lead his side at Headingley despite working through a brief net session.

"Babar Azam is not available, Salman will be captain," head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said on Tuesday.

"It's not broken, there is a little bit of swelling on the finger. Hopefully he will be available for the second Test match."

Babar's absence robs Pakistan not only of their leader but one of their most talented batters, with nine Test hundreds to his name and a Test average of 43.68. Saud Shakeel is expected to be drafted into the XI after sitting out the West Indies series.

'Relaxed Root looks up for the challenge'

Sky Sports News reporter James Cole:

"It's old shoes for Joe Root; he's got all the experience behind him and he seemed relaxed.

"He is, it's fair to say, inheriting a big rebuilding job. England have lost seven of their last 10 Tests, they've lost their head coach Brendon McCullum and their captain Ben Stokes, who had been such a mainstay of the Test team for so long and led such a unique, attacking brand of cricket called Bazball.

Image: Jordan Cox comes into England's side for just his second Test

"As well as losing Stokes from the middle order, who was the glue and provided balance between the batting and bowling, they've got an opener Emilio Gay who has played just three Test and who is out of nick at the moment, and a rookie at number three in Jordan Cox, who has only batted there once before.

"In place of the talismanic Stokes, Dan Lawrence comes back in and offers a spinning all-rounder option, but he hasn't played a Test in two years.

"It's fair to say Root has got a lot on his hands, but he's up for the challenge."

Sports.title: Rodri completes Barcelona move as Man City pursue replacement
Sports.content:
Barcelona have confirmed the signing of Rodri from Manchester City in a deal worth £65.4m.

The Spain World Cup winner and former Ballon d'Or winner, who helped City win four Premier League titles and a Champions League crown, has signed a four-year contract with the LaLiga club.

Rodri, 30, had one year left on his City contract and, while they wanted him to stay and sign an extension, Barcelona's third offer proved to be too good to turn down.

Barcelona had bids of £40m and £55m rejected by City before the deal was eventually agreed.

Enzo Maresca's side are pursuing replacements for both Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders, who is set to join Saudi Arabian side Al Qadsiah for around £51m.
