World.title: EU supports repatriation of unaccompanied migrant minors from Ceuta to Morocco
World.content:
The European Commission confirmed on Tuesday that all people illegally remaining in Ceuta would be returned following the massive migrant influx that took place in late July.

 

"The priority is now for the Spanish and for the Moroccan authorities to maintain control of the situation and to ensure a swift return of all those who illegally remain in Ceuta", European Commission spokesperson Markus Lammert said Tuesday at a press briefing.

Lammert stressed that returns are covered by EU law, adding that they are regulated under "the return directive" and soon the "EU return regulation".

There are also provisions for the return of migrants illegally staying in the territory, including unaccompanied minors, he said.

Last week, Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska estimated that there were approximately 5,000 illegal migrants remaining in Ceuta, including 1,898 minors.

Spanish authorities have pledged to return all those illegally in Ceuta to their country of origin, saying that no one would be transferred to mainland Spain.

Earlier this month, Moroccan authorities had said they were ready to cooperate with Spain and other EU partners to facilitate the returns of unaccompanied migrants.

In addition, Lammert said the European Commission was banking on prevention and deterrence moving forward, working with platforms and fact-checkers "to counter criminal networks spreading disinformation" and "to strengthen the fight against migrant smuggling".

He said that several accounts linked to smuggling have already been closed.

Meanwhile, writing on X on Monday, European Commissioner Magnus Brunner said that Spain was doing "important and necessary work" securing the EU's shared external borders.

Brunner also reiterated the EU's readiness to deploy Frontex and Europol.

According to Spanish estimates, around 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta on 30 July, with almost all of them since returned to Morocco.

World.title: This new budget airline is launching direct flights to Spain’s Santiago de Compostela
World.content:
Planning on walking the Camino de Santiago during 2027’s Holy Year? We have good news, as those finishing up their pilgrimage will soon have a more affordable way home with the launch of a new budget airline.

 

Fly2Galicia is set to launch flights from Santiago–Rosalía de Castro Airport to eight destinations in Europe, with the first departures set for 1 December, 2026.

Domestically, the carrier will fly from Alicante, Grenada and Zaragoza, while international connections include Brussels, Prague, Munich, Venice and Milan.

Tickets went on sale today, with prices from Milan to Santiago from €41; from Brussels, Prague or Venice from €51; and from Munich starting from €71.

It should be noted that Fly2Galicia won’t actually operate these initial flights, which will instead be run by another European operator which has yet to be named.

The news comes after Wizz Air announced it would be launching flights to Santiago from Rome and Warsaw this December.

The carrier will launch a permanent base at the airport in February, which will also see the launch of domestic routes to Malaga, Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Fuerteventura and Zaragoza.

What to do in Santiago de Compostela

Wander around Santiago de Compostela’s UNESCO-listed Old Town to discover why it has been described as “one of the world's most beautiful urban areas”, with architectural styles ranging from Romanesque and Gothic to Baroque and Neoclassicist.

Grab fresh seafood and produce from Mercado de Abastos food market, best washed down with a glass of Albariño, the white wine Galicia is known for.

Outside of the region’s capital, you can visit other cities like A Coruña and Vigo, or head to the Rías Baixas, which is known for its beaches and islands.

World.title: Minors living alone on Ceuta's streets at risk of abuse
World.content:
Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.

It's 8 a.m. at the Tarajal industrial park in the autonomous city of Ceuta. But there are no workers and truck drivers to be seen near the warehouses today. Instead, there are makeshift tents, some of them made out of cardboard, with mainly children and teenagers sleeping under dirty blankets.

According to certain estimates, there could be between 3,000 and 5,000 unaccompanied minors in Ceuta. Some are living on the streets because they cannot find a spot in one of the already overcrowded reception facilities in the enclave.

Amina (not her real name), a 14-year-old Moroccan girl, and her brother were among the 80,000 people who crossed the border into Spain from Morocco in late July. Though most of these have since left Ceuta, some 9,000 remain, according to the local authorities — and many are minors. "

What's worst is that we don't have toilets," said Amina. "We have to go somewhere in the bushes, but I don't dare go alone."

Close by is a Moroccan woman called Malika (also not her real name) who has spread out several blankets for herself and her four children. She told DW she was not making enough as a cleaning lady in Morocco, adding that she earned the equivalent of €7 ($8) per day.

"That's just not enough to provide for everyone," she said. "School will start again soon, and I don't have any money for books, nor even decent clothes for the children."

That's why she decided to take part in the mass crossing of the Spanish border last month when she read about it on social media. But now she doesn't know what to do.

Malika said she does not know what to do now that she is in Ceuta Image: Zhor Baki/DW

"One child got sick. He had a high fever, but I couldn't get help anywhere," she said. In the end, she made compresses with water and vinegar to see if that would help.

But now she is particularly worried about her 12-and 14-year-old daughters, because the number of sexual assaults has risen sharply in the past week. Police are currently investigating at least 15 suspected cases of rape. The local authorities suspect the actual number of cases to be much higher.

Conditions particularly difficult for girls

Susana Ascaso, an emergency doctor at Ceuta University Hospital, said she had treated several young girls in recent days.

"Just yesterday, another 12-year-old came to the emergency room," she said. "She said that other migrants had harassed her and touched her inappropriately. She arrived here completely terrified and in tears. She was with a woman who had found her on the street. That woman saved the girl."

Ascaso said conditions were particularly difficult for "girls under 18" who were "particularly at risk." She added that there was a major imbalance in the numbers of male and female migrants. "That doesn't help, of course."

Did Morocco instigate the Ceuta migrant incident? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Several high-ranking politicians in Ceuta have called for more support from the central government in the Spanish capital, Madrid. Nabila Benzina, the regional minister for health and social affairs, told DW that the current crisis was the "worst moment in Ceuta's history" and said more police officers were needed in the enclave. "Especially to protect young women, but also for the general protection of the population."

Ceuta's president, Juan Jesus Vivas, spoke of a "high-risk situation," in which it was increasingly difficult to maintain public services. "As far as minors are concerned, we are currently 5,000% over capacity," he said. "That means nobody can look after them adequately."

'I'd like to be an architect one day'

The Spanish government has announced plans to transfer unaccompanied minors to the mainland but there is no concrete timeline. Several regions, in which the far-right Vox party is part of the government, have said they refuse to take in any migrants.

Vivas told DW that the minors should be "reunited with their families. Otherwise, the Moroccan social services should assume responsibility for them." He said this was the only solution, adding that Madrid should put the "appropriate legal proceedings" in motion.

Ceuta migrant surge puts pressure on Spain, Morocco To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Many of the minors in Ceuta said they do not want to go back to Morocco or elsewhere in Africa despite the conditions in Ceuta.

Ibrahim, a 7-year-old child from Sudan, said he would not give up until he could provide "a better life for his parents back home." Amina, 14, also said she would not go back to Morocco.

"The schools here are really bad. I want a different future for myself. I'd like to become an architect someday," she said.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Nigeria: Dozens killed in Plateau state attack
World.content:
Officials in Nigeria have said at least 25 people were killed in their homes when armed men stormed their village Monday night. Fears of reprisal are real as violence between Muslim herders and Christian farmers spirals.

Local officials say at least 25 people were murdered on Monday night by armed men who stormed the village of Bin-Per, in the Mangu local government area of Nigeria's Plateau state.

Perpetrators reportedly moved from house to house, killing residents with machetes.

Women and children accounted for most of the victims.

Resident Muftwan Yamput told France's AFP news agency that he and his family "survived by a whisker."

"But," he added, "my neighbors were attacked. Two people killed in their house."

Cycle of reprisals in Nigeria attacks

Monday night's massacre followed the killing of two herders last week.

Those were in turn followed by a suspected reprisal targeting the nearby village of Maitimbe, where multiple houses were torched.

The Mwaghavul Youth Movement, a local ⁠advocacy group, ​has accused authorities of ​failing to protect vulnerable communities.

"The ‌recurring destruction of communities, killing of innocent citizens, burning of homes and destruction of farmlands cannot continue ​to be treated ⁠as ordinary incidents," said the group's spokesperson on Sunday while calling for a review of security ​in the area.

Matthew Kwarpo, a representative in the Plateau state assembly, called on authorities to, "deploy proactive measures in preventing or mitigating unnecessary attacks before they occur," especially in Mangu.

"The incident underscores the urgent need for concerted efforts to address the underlying grievances and prevent further escalation of violence in the affected communities," said Kwarpo.

The Fulani land dispute: Impact in northern Nigeria To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Amnesty says President Tinubu not fulfilling promise to 'enhance security'

The incidents of the last week are the continuation of years of spiraling violence between nomadic Muslim ethnic Fulani herders and mainly Christian farmers over access to increasingly scarce land and resources in central Nigeria's Middle Belt region.

Land grabbing over mineral and mining resources, political and economic tensions between locals and outsiders, and the influx of hardline Muslim and Christian preachers have all fueled divisions.

Plateau has also seen hundreds killed in urban riots between religious groups in recent years.

In May 2025, rights group Amnesty International (AI) estimated that at least 2,630 people had been killed in Plateau state alone in the two years since President Bola Tinubu had taken office on the promise of enhancing security.

The group said authorities had instead failed "to protect the rights to life, physical integrity, liberty and the security of tens of thousands of people across the country."

World.title: Middle East: No talks or conversations with Iran, Trump says
World.content:
Skip next section 6 killed in Israeli strike on Gaza, Palestinian officials say

08/18/2026 August 18, 2026 6 killed in Israeli strike on Gaza, Palestinian officials say

An Israeli airstrike on a cafe in Gaza City on Tuesday killed six people and wounded a dozen more, Palestinian officials said, while the Israeli military said it carried out an attack targeting Hamas commanders.

Mahmoud Bassal, a spokesperson for Gaza's civil defence agency, told AFP that at least six were killed, "including a child, and a large number were wounded, as a result of an Israeli raid on tents of displaced people in Gaza port."

An eyewitness told AFP Israeli war planes fired two missiles at the "Sweet and Bitter" cafe on the fishermen's port.

The Reuters news agency cited Palestinian medics as saying 14 others were wounded in the missile attack on the small cafe.

The Israeli army said it carried out a "precise aerial strike" against "several Hamas commanders" who "planned to carry out terror attacks against [Israeli military] troops operating in the Gaza Strip" and that "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians."

Strike comes as Trump pushes for Gaza peace

The strikes came just one day after US President Donald Trump's envoy Jared Kushner was in Israel and met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Israel has insisted it will not withdraw from the areas it still controls in Gaza, some 60% of the Palestinian enclave, until Hamas has fully disarmed.

Hamas, which Israel, the US and other countries designate as a terrorist organization, has expressed its intention to disarm, but sticking points remain including over where the arms would then go.

After the Tuesday attack, Hamas said it exemplified Israel's "blatant disregard for all calls for a ceasefire issued by mediators and guarantor states."

World.title: Afghanistan: Only 5% of labor market are women under Taliban
World.content:
The International Labour Organization estimates that only 5.1% of workers in Afghanistan are women, five years after the Taliban's return to power. That's less than a third of the proportion in 2019 and 2020.

The share of women in Afghanistan's labor market has falled to around one worker in 20 in the five years since the Taliban returned to power, according to a report published by the International Labour Organization (ILO) on Tuesday .

"Afghanistan is estimated to have the second lowest female labor force participation rate worldwide, at only 5.1% in 2026, against the backdrop of severe restrictions in women's access to education and employment," the ILO wrote.

It called for urgent steps to counter women's "severe exclusion," also saying this was essential to buttress the Afghan economy's resilience more generally.

The Taliban rapidly returned to power in August 2021 amid a pullout by the US and other NATO forces, ending a 20-year period when women enjoyed comparatively improved economic and educational liberty after years of hardline Islamist rule.

Afghanistan's leaders have been marking the fifth anniversary of the Taliban's return to power this month Image: Javid Ashna/Middle East Images/picture alliance

What did the ILO say about women in Afghanistan's labor market?

The UN organization warned of "significant demographic and institutional changes" in the labor market since 2021, many of them disadvantaging women.

Female labor force participation had dipped from 16.5% in 2020 to 5.1% in 2026

That's the second lowest rate on the planet, only ahead of wartorn Yemen

Young women "NEETs" — people "not in education, employment or training" — represented 84% of the cohort, compared to 76% in 2020 and 68% in 2019

Among young men, the NEET figure was below 30%, and falling compared to the recent high-point of the COVID pandemic in 2020

The UN's Development Agency meanwhile said one rare boom area was businesses owned by women

These had increased in prevalence roughly tenfold, albeit precisely because other employment options were so scarce

"Afghanistan cannot build a resilient labor market while such a large share of its population remains excluded from economic activity," said Tite Habiyakare, senior coordinator and head of the ILO office for Afghanistan.

One boom area for women is in entrepreneurial ventures and self-employment — albeit precisely because other job options are becoming more limited Image: Saifurahman Safi/Xinhua/picture alliance

What did the ILO say about Afghanistan's economy more generally?

The report said that Afghanistan's labor market remained "under considerable pressure" five years after the Taliban takeover, having only moderately recovered from the crash of 2021.

Afghanistan's GDP tumbled by around 15% when the Taliban returned amid the COVID pandemic and western troops and funds flowed out. It remained deep in negative territory in 2022 and had just barely clawed its way into positive growth territory since, falling well short of returning to its pre-Taliban levels.

Employment numbers have started to rise in absolute terms, but not fast enough to keep up with population growth — either domestic or as a result of emigrant returns — meaning the share of people in work is flatlining at just under one-third of the population.

The paper also called for increased investment in representative labor force data-gathering, warning that its data was reliant on modeling estimates that "are subject to considerable uncertainty and should be interpreted with appropriate caution."

In Afghanistan, girls study in secret to skirt Taliban ban To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

How are external factors like the war in Iran and migrant returns impacting the situation?

Large-scale returns of emigrants, particularly from Iran and Pakistan, have become "one of the defining labor market challenges facing Afghanistan," the report said.

More than 6 million Afghans returned from Iran and Pakistan between 2023 and the end of May this year, with the surge driven "by a combination of policy, economic and security factors."

The report noted World Bank projections suggesting that this could halve the influence of remittance inflows into the Afghan economy, from around 4% of GDP in 2020 to around 2% of economic output by 2025.

"Since February 2026, the Middle East crisis has added further uncertainty for Afghans residing in Iran, alongside the continued implementation of returns policies," the ILO said.

Finally, the ILO warned that the war in Iran posed additional risks for Afghanistan — in terms of general inflation, food and fuel prices, trade and transport disruptions, and increased potential returns from Iran.

Around 70% of workers, partiularly less skilled ones, were at least moderately exposed to factors relevant to the crisis like energy prices, the report found, with roughly 30% facing only slight exposure.

It noted a steep rise in inflation figures in the past 12 months, rising from less than 1% in May 2025 to around 8% by May 2026, and warned that such increases "disproportionately affect poorer households and reduce real earnings, particularly among informal workers."

World.title: As drought hits Germany's harvest, will food prices rise?
World.content:
Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.

1. How severe is Germany's 2026 harvest decline?

The German Farmers' Association (DBV) on Tuesday warned of a "below-average" harvest due to ongoing drought that has left large areas of farmland severely parched.

In a statement, DBV President Joachim Rukwied warned that the country's grain harvest would be 7% lower than last year, blaming an "overly dry spring and a heat wave in the second half of June," which had "significantly damaged many crops."

Overall grain production was expected to be 41.9 million tons this year, the DBV said, a shortfall of some 3.3 million tons compared with 2025.

Rapeseed saw the largest fall, with 3.3 million tons harvested, nearly 17% lower than last year. Barley remained at last year's level despite a lower yield, as more land was used to grow the crop.

The potato crop was also expected to be below average and some regions would see a "significantly worse" harvest for sugar beet, DBV said.

Rukwied noted how location played a bigger role in determining crop yields this year than usual, and pointed to poor crop yields and even crop failures, particularly in southern and western Germany.

German farmers face harvest losses, price uncertainty To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Separately, Germany's Federal Statistical Office warned that the country's apple harvest was forecast to drop 18% compared with last year.

Germany is experiencing a severe drought during a summer of frequent record-breaking temperatures, which has exacerbated the effects of below-average rainfall since March, according to the German Weather Service.

2. How will the drought affect food prices and availability?

Agriculture Minister Alois Rainer said Tuesday that the government isn't expecting a sudden or sharp increase in food prices as a result of the lower harvest.

"I don't expect prices to rise immediately because food prices also depend on many other factors — the supply chain, transportation and production," he told public broadcaster ZDF.

The German Raiffeisen Association, which represents 1,600 agricultural cooperatives, also said last week a large hike in prices was unlikely.

In Germany, some fields have suffered total or near-total crop failure due to drought and excessive heat Image: Frank Hoermann/SvenSimon/picture alliance

However, the large falls in rapeseed and sugar beet production could reduce domestic supply of oil and sugar, requiring imports to make up the shortfall.

Local media reported last week that the drought was also causing animal feed stocks to fall drastically in several states, particularly in southern Germany.

The German Farmers' Association has previously warned that lower grain yields and weaker grassland growth could push up prices for feed, meat, milk and eggs

In the hardest-hit areas of the country, potatoes and other vegetables could become more expensive as supply tightens. For most shoppers, however, the main impact is more likely to be gradual price increases rather than shortages.

3. How does this drought fit into wider food security concerns?

Farming, both at home and globally, has faced repeated pressures since the COVID-19 pandemic.

German food prices have risen by over 36% since 2020, according to government data published last month.

The price hikes were especially strong for poultry meat, many dairy products and eggs, edible fats and oils, and sugar, the government calculated.

Russia's war in Ukraine disrupted Black Sea exports of Ukrainian grain in 2022 and drove energy prices higher, impacting the cost of fertilizer, transport and food processing.

More recently, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran war prevented oil, gas and fertilizer ingredients from leaving the Gulf.

The conflict has pushed up prices of diesel fuel, fertilizers and pesticides, with some farmers cutting back on soil nutrients.

Compounding crises over the past six years have left large parts of the German agriculture sector financially stretched, the industry has warned. Many farmers have said they face much higher costs and rising debts, and have limited room to absorb further losses.

In previous years, farmers have used tractors to blockade roads to pressure the government for help Image: Daniel Bockwoldt/dpa/picture alliance

4. What support are German farmers seeking?

The German Farmers' Association said some farmers may need interim financing to secure their futures. Rukwied called on Berlin to launch an "immediate package" to help support the agriculture sector.

Recommendations include boosting the European Union's fertilizer aid package from €60 million to €180 million ($208 million), paid out quickly and without red tape.

DBV also called on ministers to cut the tax on agricultural diesel, at least until the end of November.

For several months from late 2023, German farmers blocked highways with tractors over plans to scrap fuel subsidies for the agricultural sector, which were later partially reversed.

Agriculture Minister Rainer on Tuesday promised targeted help to farmers, but only when reliable official figures are available at the end of August.

Edited by: Tim Rooks

World.title: Dressed for power: Giorgia Meloni and the language of fashion
World.content:
From Giorgia Meloni's shift from dark suits to pastels to Angela Merkel's signature jackets, politicians have long used clothing to shape how voters see them. In this day and age, power dressing has evolved.

Often dressing in pastel colors, with wide-legged pants falling over her high heels, Italy's first female prime minister can't escape fashion scrutiny — and not only because Giorgia Meloni is the leader of the world's fashion capital.

"Fashion is a language — it tells us what its wearer wants to say without any actual words," Michela Bonafoni, who teaches fashion at Unicollege in Florence, told DW.



"Perhaps what you wear is very close to your personality. But if you want to give a different impression of yourself, you can also do this through clothing — this is what Meloni does constantly," explained Bonafoni.

Meloni began her tenure as prime minister wearing dark suits ,as seen in this photo from December 2022 Image: IRAQI PRIME MINISTER'S PRESS OFFICE /AFP

Meloni's clothing style can be read as part of a broader political transition: from outsider to establishment figure. When she first took office in 2022, her appearance was closely tied to the political identity she had built as a leader of the right-wing Brothers of Italy party with post-fascist roots. Her look: dark suits with chunky boots, serious and even combative.

Enter the concept of "power dressing," which emerged in the 1970s and became influential in the 1980s, as second-wave feminism coincided with more women entering professional and managerial roles. The suit became a way for women to signal authority in traditionally male workplaces.

Italian designer Giorgio Armani played a key role — his softer, more fluid tailoring offered a new version of the power suit — borrowing from menswear while creating a more feminine language of authority.

During her first official public appearances, Meloni was often seen in dark Armani suits, a nod to traditional power dressing, and a look that said, according to Bonafoni: "I'm here in this kind of government and that's all there is to it."

From masculine suits to pastels

Since then, Meloni's look has softened — she's often seen in wide-legged silhouettes and suits in cream, beige, pink and other muted or pastel shades. The style change also coincides with how she has become a more established figure in European politics, moving closer to the European Union and becoming a prominent supporter of Ukraine.

Yet, Meloni has maintained a conservative approach to domestic politics, which hasn't gone down well with much of the public — including many in the country's fashion industry. No luxury brand, including Armani, has publicly stepped forward to style her or support her use of their clothing.

This hasn't stopped Meloni from using fashion to appeal to a broader public. "When Meloni understood that many Italians didn't like some of the actions of her government, she started to wear the pastel colors, which incite understanding and say 'I'm Giorgia, a woman who is kind,'" said Bonafoni. The author also pointed out that Meloni sports "Made in Italy" designers as part of her brand of nationalism — attaching its power to her own.

Today, Meloni (seen here meeting German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in June) often wears wide trousers and softer colors Image: Chris Emil Janßen/picture alliance

At the Salone del Mobile, Italy's premier design event in Milan this past April, Meloni chose an informal look: jeans and a casual beige blazer.

"Her look said: I'm casual because I'm just like you — but I'm also exactly where I want to be right now in this moment and in this government," said Bonafoni. Such a style exudes confidence and is closer to the more relaxed style of female politicians in the US, Bonafoni added.

Merkel wore a distinctive 'uniform' during the years she served as Germany's chancellor Image: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

A political 'uniform'

But political power doesn't always require a changing wardrobe. For some female leaders, consistency itself can become a form of power dressing.

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel developed one of the most recognizable wardrobes in modern politics. Her formula was remarkably consistent: trousers and a three-button jacket, with the jackets appearing in an extraordinary range of colors. The simplicity itself became a kind of uniform, putting Merkel herself, as a politician, rather than her fashion, at the center.

"Her 'second skin' of clothing was very close to her character, her attitudes and political decisions she made," said Bonafoni.





Former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher also had her fashion uniforms so to speak, down pat. Her appearance was carefully constructed — tailored suits, pearls, handbags — an instantly recognizable version of feminine political authority in her era.

These days, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum offers another prime example of a politician who uses clothing to send a message. She frequently wears garments made by women artisans from Mexico to show her support and solidarity with Mexico's Indigenous communities.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is known for wearing clothing made by women in Indigenous communities Image: Carlos Santiago/Eyepix Group/IMAGO

From hipster dad to tactical wear

While the few women politicians we have on the world stage fall under increased fashion scrutiny, men too have long understood the political power of appearance — perhaps now more than ever. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy often chooses to wear tactical clothing that's far from the standard suit and tie look of most world leaders.

As Ukrainian journalist Illia Ponomarenko told Politico last year, it's part of his anti-elitist message, one that directly confronts the world leaders he meets. "His clothes are basically asking: What are you about? Are you about the business of saving lives, or are you about fancy protocols?" said Ponomarenko. "Even when he meets with kings, he dresses in a way that represents the average Ukrainian involved in this war effort. So it's a message to say, 'I've come to the corners of power as a representative of my humble people.'"

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (right) and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham (left) opt for more casual looks Image: Press Service Of The President Of Ukraine/SvenSimon/picture alliance



Similarly, the UK's Labour Party Prime Minister Andy Burnham, whose look has been referred to as "hipster dad," chooses smart-casual styles; T-shirts, polo shirts and trainers. It's a political messaging move that says he's on the same level as the public.



As for Giorgia Meloni, Bonafoni expects the world will soon see another style change as she is challenged by far-right politician and former army general Roberto Vannacci.

"Meloni has said she doesn't want Vannacci in her government, but her party will need him in a coalition if it wants to remain in power," said Bonafoni. "I'm sure if and when Vannacci challenges her, she will change her style again because she'll have to present herself as someone who's even more powerful."

Edited by: Tenzin Sekhon

World.title: Syria, US condemn Israeli strikes on military base
World.content:
Israel has not officially claimed the strikes on Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib, some 70 kilometers from the Turkish border. US envoy Tom Barrack called the Israeli strikes an "unnecessary escalation."

Eight Israeli airstrikes hit an unused airbase in northwestern Syria's Idlib province early on Tuesday, Syrian state media reported, in attacks widely condemned by Damascus and Washington.

The attacks struck the runway and storage facilities at Abu al-Duhur base, Syrian state-run broadcaster Al-Ikhbariya reported, some 70 kilometers (43.5 miles) from the Turkish border.

Turkey is a key ally of Syria's interim government, in power since ousting former President Bashar Assad in a December 2024 lightning offensive.

What else do we know about the Israeli airstrikes on the Idlib airbase?

Syrian state media, quoting a military source, said that "Israeli occupation aircraft early this morning targeted the runway" of the base "with eight strikes," damaging infrastructure but without causing casualties.

The facility has been out of service as a dedicated military base for over a decade. The Reuters news agency cited an unnamed military source as saying it has been used as a training center for Syria's new army since Assad's 2024 ouster.

Israel has yet to officially comment on the attacks.

They come on the heels of a Turkish military delegation's visit to the airfield, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights monitor. According to the UK-based monitor, the visit was part of efforts to reactivate the base.

The strikes caused damage but Syrian media reported they left no casualties Image: REUTERS

How did the US, Syria react to the attacks?

Tom Barrack, US ambassador to Turkey and special presidential envoy for Syria and Iraq, condemned the Israeli strikes in a post on X.

"We are deeply concerned that the confirmed Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Airbase constitute an unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability," Barrack wrote.

He defended Syria's interim administration of Ahmed al-Sharaa, who once led an Al-Qaeda-affiliated militant group but has since distanced himself from Islamist militancy. Barrack stressed Sharaa's administration "repeatedly indicated a preference for de-escalation with Israel."

"We encourage all parties to prioritize logical discourse over further military incidents," he said.

Netanyahu's endless wars: How dangerous are they for Israel? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Syria's Foreign Ministry also condemned the strikes, calling them "an unjustified act of aggression."

It urged the international community and the United Nations Security Council to "take a firm position against Israel's repeated violations of Syrian sovereignty."

The "continuation of these Israeli attacks" since December 2024 came while Syria "has exercised restraint and worked to consolidate stability and avoid escalation," it added.

Turkey also strongly condemned the Israeli airstrikes, calling on "the international community to ⁠take ​a ​more decisive stance to ​end Israel's ‌escalating aggression against Syria."

Tense Israeli-Turkish relations overshadowed by Syria

Since Assad's ouster, Israel has launched hundreds of strikes on Syria, sending troops to a United Nations-patrolled buffer zone that had separated Israeli and Syrian forces in Syria's Israeli-occupied Golan since 1974.

How Golan Heights Druze community views post-Assad Syria To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The Israeli army has also carried out regular incursions deeper inside Syrian territory.

Israeli officials have declared their intention to keep forces in a self-declared "security zone" in southern Syria.

Turkey has accused Israel of trying to destabilize Syria and its new administration, which Ankara has been helping by training its army and assisting with building its state institutions and infrastructure.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz has directly warned Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, stressing Israel would now allow steps that strengthen Syria's military capabilities in ways that could threaten Israel.

World.title: Should India be worried about the Mecca defense pact?
World.content:
A defense agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey brings Islamabad deeper into the security architecture of the Middle East. How is India planning to respond?

The "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement" signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on August 7, comes amid the Iran war and shifting security arrangements in the Middle East.

Saudi Arabia is seeking additional security partnerships as it faces uncertainty over the reliability of the US security umbrella. Turkey is seeking a larger regional role, while Pakistan is looking to turn its longstanding military relationship with Riyadh into wider strategic influence.

The agreement calls for collective defense, stating an armed attack on one member will be regarded as an attack on all three.

It also formalizes relationships that already exist. Pakistan has trained and assisted Saudi forces for decades, while its defense relationship with Turkey has expanded through military exchanges and cooperation.

For India, the question is whether the pact gives archrival Pakistan a deeper role in a region central to Indian interests.

Pact changes little on the ground for India

Some Indian analysts see little immediate change in the regional balance. Others see a warning that India needs a stronger security presence in a region where its economic interests have grown considerably.

India has ramped up defense spending in recent years Image: Adnan Abidi/REUTERS

Saudi Arabia is a major energy and investment partner for New Delhi. The Gulf and the Red Sea are vital to India's trade and energy security.

The pact allows Pakistan to expand on its security role in the Gulf while providing an institutional framework for closer defense cooperation and potentially greater access to funding and technology.

However, former Indian High Commissioner to Pakistan Ajay Bisaria believes the agreement will have little effect on the basic dynamics of an India Pakistan confrontation.

"The Mecca pact is not worth the paper it's written on," Bisaria told DW.

"It does little to move the needle beyond the Saudi-Pakistan defense pact of last year, an arrangement that proved to have only signaling value for Iran, the US and Israel, at a moment when Riyadh was unsettled by the frailty of the American security umbrella," he added.

In the event of a future India-Pakistan crisis, the former ambassador said he does not expect the pact to fundamentally alter Saudi Arabia's position.

"For India, this is a pact to be monitored, not one to be unduly concerned about," Bisaria said.

"In the event of another terrorist attack from Pakistan, the situation is unlikely to look very different from Operation Sindoor, save, perhaps, for some added rhetoric," he said, referring to the name of India's response to a 2025 attack on tourists in Kashmir that New Delhi has blamed on Pakistan-backed militants. Islamabad has denied any involvement in the attack.

"Turkey would continue to supply drones and equipment to Pakistan, while the Saudis, far from rushing to position themselves as its defenders, are more likely to offer their services, more vocally, as mediators," he said.

No immediate concern for India

Tara Kartha, former member of the National Security Council Secretariat, believes India should not overstate the significance of the agreement.

"India doesn't need to be overly concerned about the Mecca pact. Saudi Arabia and Turkey hardly see us as a strategic competitor or an 'enemy'," Kartha told DW.

Much of the Pakistan-Turkey military relationship already exists, Kartha added. "Turkey's formidable defense industry will certainly be made available for the pact's constituents," she said.

"But Pakistan and Turkey already have a strong defense relationship including joint development of the Kaan aircraft. So, nothing really changes on the ground barring possibly increased funding for the Pakistan defense budget. That is certainly a problem that can't be easily circumvented," she said.

The more immediate concern for India may be whether Saudi resources and Turkish technology could strengthen Pakistan's military capabilities over time.

India's ties with Saudi Arabia

Beyond the India-Pakistan rivalry, the pact also raises questions about India's ties with Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom has built a substantial relationship with India, spanning energy, investment, trade and political ties. And Riyadh's effort to diversify its security partnerships does not necessarily mean choosing Pakistan over India.

Geopolitical analyst Harsh Pant, vice president at the Delhi-based Observer Research Foundation, told DW that India should respond cautiously but not passively.

"The different strategic interests of the three members could limit the pact's cohesion, but New Delhi should use its own relationship with Riyadh to deepen security, intelligence and economic cooperation," Pant said.

Deeper bilateral ties with Saudi Arabia, he added, could help ensure that Pakistan's new role does not translate into disproportionate influence in the Gulf.

New Delhi will also have to watch the military dimension closely. If Turkish drones, missiles, electronic warfare systems or other defense technologies become more readily available to Pakistan, India's western security calculations could change.

What's behind Pakistan's deepening ties with Saudi Arabia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

A wake-up call for India?

Randhir Jaiswal, spokesperson for India's Ministry of External Affairs, said New Delhi was examining the pact's implications "from the perspective of India's national security and considerations of regional peace and stability."

"India remains fully committed to safeguarding its national interests and will take all necessary measures in this regard," he said.

Strategic expert C. Raja Mohan told DW that the trilateral agreement points to a larger problem in India's approach to the Gulf. India's economic dependence on the region has grown considerably, while its security presence has remained comparatively limited, he said.

"For India, this should be a warning that New Delhi cannot remain primarily a diplomatic and economic player in the Gulf. It needs greater military reach in the region and deeper, practical security and defense relationships with individual Middle Eastern countries," Mohan said.

He sees a widening mismatch between India's interests and its security presence.

"The gap between India's economic interests and its limited military-security presence is becoming harder to ignore," he added.

India could deepen defense and intelligence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states, strengthen maritime security in the Arabian Sea and Red Sea, and closely monitor Pakistan-Turkey military cooperation.

Mohan, a professor of American Studies at Jindal Global University, sees the agreement principally as an attempt by Saudi Arabia to widen its options.

"I see it more as evidence of the Arab states' continuing inability to build a dependable regional security system and, importantly, as Saudi Arabia hedging against uncertainty over the reliability of the US security umbrella," Mohan said.

Edited by: Wesley Rahn

World.title: Trump declara el estrecho de Ormuz “nuevo territorio de Estados Unidos”
World.content:
Primero fueron Groenlandia y el canal de Panamá. Después, Canadá e incluso Venezuela. Ahora el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha incluido al estrecho de Ormuz en su lista cada vez más larga en este mandato de territorios bajo soberanía ajena o internacional de los que dice que quiere anexionarse.

Desde su regreso a la Casa Blanca, Trump ha hecho alarde de una política expansionista en la que declara, entre otras cosas, la supremacía estadounidense en el continente americano. Y no duda en poner sus miras en otros puntos del planeta. Ya había sorprendido la semana pasada cuando, en una declaración, aseguró que el estratégico cuello de botella marítimo, la clave de su guerra contra Irán, se convertiría en territorio estadounidense. Este martes ha dejado claro que no es una idea pasajera o una broma de un momento. En un mensaje en su red social, Truth, el republicano ha publicado una fotografía con esta denominación.

En la imagen se ve un mapa del estrecho que separa el golfo Pérsico del de Omán. En ella marca el estrecho de Ormuz con un círculo y añade el lema “NUEVO Territorio de Estados Unidos”, acompañado de una franja azul, roja y blanca con estrellas.

Publicación de Donald Trump en Truth sobre el estrecho de Ormuz , el 18 de agosto de 2026.

En otro mensaje posterior en su red social, el mandatario ha vuelto a referirse al paso marítimo y al estancamiento de las negociaciones de paz entre Washington y Teherán. “No hay conversaciones ni charlas en marcha, o previstas, con la República Islámica de Irán. El bloqueo naval sigue en pleno efecto y fuerza. El estrecho de Ormuz está abierto y operativo. Todas las minas acuáticas han sido retiradas o detonadas”.

Ya el pasado viernes Trump aseguró que planteaba incorporar el estrecho de Ormuz como “territorio de Estados Unidos” tras “derrotar a Irán”. Aunque las negociaciones siguen estancadas y el plazo que los dos países se dieron en junio para llegar a un acuerdo de paz definitivo expiró este lunes sin pena ni gloria, el presidente insiste en proclamar que su país es el vencedor militar absoluto del conflicto.

“Después de que terminemos de derrotar a Irán, que está siendo derrotado muy gravemente, muy pronto declararé el estrecho de Ormuz territorio de Estados Unidos, en esencia. Tenemos un bloqueo. Ningún barco pasa a menos que nosotros queramos que pase”, había declarado el republicano en un mítin celebrado en Long Island (Nueva York).

Una idea ya mencionada

Unos días antes el mandatario estadounidense ya mencionó la idea de que Estados Unidos se “quede” el estrecho de Ormuz argumentando que ya controla la ruta marítima porque los ataques estadounidenses realizados desde febrero han diezmado las capacidades militares iraníes, algo que Teherán ha rechazado.

“Estados Unidos tiene el control total del estrecho de Ormuz. ¡Creo que nos lo quedaremos!“, escribió el miércoles pasado Trump en Truth Social, asegurando que “no hay nada que Irán pueda hacer al respecto”.

No está claro cómo el presidente pretende pasar de las amenazas a los hechos. Mediante la voluntad de la población afectada parece sumamente improbable. Pero la fuerza tampoco parece una opción. Una operación militar de conquista convertiría la guerra actual en una escena de paz y amor en una comuna hippie. Hoy por hoy, Estados Unidos no cuenta con munición suficiente para algo así, después de haber vaciado sus arsenales en los combates de los últimos meses. Y el Departamento de Defensa se plantea una reducción de la presencia militar estadounidense en Oriente Próximo una vez haya concluido esta guerra, ante los daños que sus bases en la zona han sufrido tras meses de hostilidades con Irán, según ha publicado este martes el periódico The Washington Post.

El Mando Central, responsable de las operaciones militares estadounidenses en Oriente Próximo, mantiene desplegados habitualmente cerca de 40.000 soldados en una veintena de emplazamientos desde Jordania a Omán. Pero la guerra contra Irán ha disparado la presencia militar de Estados Unidos en la zona, reforzada ahora con buques, sistemas de defensa antiaérea, aviones de combate y otros tipos de armamento.

El estrecho de Ormuz, una de las principales rutas mundiales para el transporte de petróleo y gas, es un corredor de aguas internacionales limitado en el norte por Irán y en el sur por Omán. Aunque este sultanato fue víctima el lunes de las amenazas de Trump, que advirtió que si el país continúa sus contactos con Teherán para establecer algún tipo de mecanismo de peaje en el estrecho lo bombardería sin piedad, Omán es un firme aliado de Washington en la zona del Golfo, y una serie de acuerdos bilaterales permiten a las fuerzas estadounidenses acceder a sus puertos y aeródromos militares.

La incertidumbre sobre el futuro del estrecho —uno de los asuntos que las negociaciones de 60 días debían resolver— parece ser el motivo que ha impelido al mandatario a su provocadora reclamación territorial. El paso de mercancías y petróleo representa una mínima proporción del volumen previo al conflicto. Cada vez menos barcos se atreven a atravesarlo. Este martes, un barco mercante fue atacado por un “proyectil desconocido” cuando trataba de dejar atrás el golfo Pérsico a través de las aguas omaníes en el estrecho, según la agencia de Operaciones Comerciales Marítimas del Reino Unido. La sala de motores del navío quedó dañada y el servicio de Guardacostas de Omán tuvo que acudir a rescatar a los miembros de la tripulación.

Pero Trump insiste una y otra vez en que, gracias a las fuerzas estadounidenses, el paso marítimo (que había estado abierto sin ningún tipo de problema hasta que empezó la guerra el 28 de febrero) está desbloqueado y se puede atravesar con normalidad.

Ante las intenciones de Irán de imponer un sistema de peaje a los buques que lo crucen, en colaboración con Omán, el presidente estadounidense también ha coqueteado en algunas declaraciones con la idea de que sea su país el que imponga algún tipo de tarifa. Una propuesta que se da de bruces con décadas de política oficial de Washington, que se presenta como adalid de la libertad de navegación y que para defenderla ha llevado a cabo regularmente patrullas en puntos como el mar del Sur de China.

Este lunes venció el plazo de 60 días que se dieron EE UU e Irán con la firma de un memorando de entendimiento el pasado 17 de junio, que declaraba el “cese inmediato y permanente de las operaciones militares en todos los frentes”, como parte de un proceso para negociar el fin de la guerra en Oriente Próximo. Ninguna de las dos partes ha expresado interés en aplicar la prórroga contemplada en el documento de 14 puntos. En declaraciones desde el Despacho Oval el lunes, Trump aseguraba que no tiene ningún interés en mantener con vida un proceso que nunca llegó a ponerse realmente en marcha.

World.title: Un profesor en Boston devuelve a México más de 1.100 piezas prehispánicas
World.content:
Más de 40 alumnos de preparatoria participaron en el proceso de clasificación de los objetos antes de ser entregados en el consulado mexicano

México crece su lista de recuperación de arte prehispánico, una política impulsada por el expresidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador y continuada por la gestión de Claudia Sheinbaum. El profesor y arqueólogo de la escuela secundaria Farmington, Jeremy Pilve, ha entregado voluntariamente al consulado de Boston 1.132 piezas arqueológicas del patrimonio cultural mexicano. En una ceremonia, Pilve ha restituido malacates —figuras circulares usadas como contrapeso en el huso— recipientes de cerámica, fragmentos de figurillas y dientes de tiburón. Ya son más de 3.700 objetos repatriados desde el comienzo del sexenio.

El profesor Pilver entregó junto al acervo documentación sobre la procedencia, las dataciones y otros datos útiles para la investigación arqueológica. Parte de esa información la ha obtenido con la ayuda de más de 40 estudiantes de preparatoria que participaron durante dos años en la clasificación, limpieza superficial, catalogación, elaboración de un inventario y base de datos digital, registro fotográfico, documentación y embalaje profesional de la colección para su restitución. La Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores no ha detallado cómo Pilve llegó a poseer las piezas.

Jeremy Pilver, a la izquierda, en la entrega de los bienes en el Consulado de México en Boston, este lunes. Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores

El conjunto de objetos es de temporalidad diversa, aunque se ha identificado que procede del sureste del país. Se trata de tiestos cerámicos alisados, modelados y pintados principalmente de uso doméstico, dos malacates completos, 18 fragmentos de figurillas, nueve lascas de obsidiana, tres pulidores de roca y 11 de sílex, así como 36 dientes de tiburón.

La restitución, según ha dicho la secretaria de Cultura, Claudia Curiel, demuestra que “la cooperación internacional, la ética y la educación” pueden contribuir a “proteger nuestro patrimonio, y a fortalecer una conciencia colectiva frente al tráfico y la apropiación indebida de los bienes de la nación”. El proceso ha sido coordinado por el propio consulado junto al Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia y la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, así como instituciones académicas de la región de Nueva Inglaterra.

Dientes de tiburón, procedentes del sureste del territorio nacional, entre los objetos recuperados. Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores

Más información Un bajorrelieve maya de más de mil años será repatriado a México desde Estados Unidos

La política es una de las señas de identidad de los Gobiernos morenistas. La Ley Federal sobre Monumentos y Zonas Arqueológicos, Artísticos e Históricos las cataloga como patrimonio nacional y obliga a promover la repatriación de las piezas que se encuentran en el extranjero. El principal obstáculo es que el éxito de esa política depende de la voluntad de colaborar de los Gobiernos de los países en los que se encuentran.

La mayor parte de las piezas recuperadas por México proceden de Estados Unidos, que encabeza la lista con más de 3.300 objetos en lo que va de mandato. Italia y Canadá le siguen muy por detrás, con la entrega de 174 y 133, respectivamente; y Francia y España están a la cola con 19 y siete devoluciones, cada uno.

World.title: Davant el dubte, els CUAP i el 061
World.content:
L’any 2025, les urgències dels hospitals públics catalans van rebre un total de 3.930.476 visites, un 2,2% más que l’any anterior.

Anar al servei d’urgències de l’hospital més proper no sempre és la millor opció. Molts problemes de salut que semblen urgents es poden resoldre de manera més eficient i ràpida trucant al 061 o optant pels Centres d’Urgències d’Atenció Primària, un senzill canvi d’hàbits que contribueix, a més, a no col·lapsar el sistema d’assistència

Qualsevol que hagi anat a parar als serveis d’urgències d’un gran hospital de l`àrea metropolitana de Barcelona un dimarts a mig matí o un divendres cap al vespre sap com de tensionada pot arribar a estar l’assistència sanitària a casa nostra en moments puntuals. Ferides obertes, lesions òssies, intoxicacions, quadres gripals, cops de calor o atacs d’ansietat conviuen en el mateix espai mentre els equips de triatge miren d’identificar els casos prioritaris i condemnen, inevitablement, la resta de pacients a llargs períodes d’espera.

L’any 2025, les urgències dels hospitals públics catalans van rebre un total de 3.930.476 visites, un 2,2% més que l’any anterior. Això s’ha traduït en un temps mitjà d’espera que frega els 47 minuts per pacient.

El 061 pot oferir un primer diagnòstic i proposta de tractament, derivar el pacient al centre més adequat, coordinar l’enviament d’un metge a casa a través del sistema d’atenció domiciliària o, si s’escau, organitzar el trasllat a urgències amb ambulància o helicòpter

La xifra pot semblar alta, però el cert és que s’ha aconseguit mantenir-la bastant estable en els últims anys, a mida que els recursos de què es disposa s’han anat adaptant a l’augment de població a Catalunya. Els experts, però, consideren que podria reduir-se de manera considerable si la ciutadania s’acostumés a fer un ús òptim de les dues grans alternatives als serveis d’urgències hospitalàries: els CUAP (Centres d’Urgències d’Atenció Primària) i el telèfon d’assistència 061.

Trucades que fan salut

El segon d’aquests recursos, el 061 Salut Respon, compta amb un equip de més 200 professionals (metges, infermers i tècnics) que garanteixen atenció sanitària no presencial i també poden proporcionar informació i consells pràctics sobre temes de salut de tot tipus. El Govern de la Generalitat va llançar l’any 2021 la campanya Creus que has d’anar a urgències? Truca al 061, per a promoure entre la població l´ús d’aquesta eina tan útil i, a dia avui, encara no tan utilitzada com caldria.

La majoria dels CUAP disposen d’instal·lacions i instrumental per a fer radiografies i analítiques, fet que garanteix la realització de les exploracions bàsiques necessàries per a obtenir un primer diagnòstic en els casos no tan urgents. Moon Safari (Getty Images)

La idea és que el ciutadà disposi d’elements de judici per a decidir si una dolència o un problema de salut concret s’han de resoldre acudint a l’hospital o poden ser tractats a distància o en un altre punt, més proper i no tan tensionat, de la xarxa assistencial. El 061 pot oferir un primer diagnòstic i proposta de tractament, derivar el pacient al centre més adequat, coordinar l’enviament d’un metge a casa a través del sistema d’atenció domiciliària o, si s’escau, organitzar el trasllat a urgències amb ambulància o helicòpter.

L’accés al servei és molt fàcil, n’hi ha prou amb marcar el número 061 o, si es contacta des de l’estranger, el 933 038 158. Ara mateix, els professionals d’aquesta xarxa atenen trucades en més de 90 idiomes i dialectes i en llengua de signes amb el seu sistema de traducció instantània, una opció que poden activar els professionals sanitaris sempre que la considerin necessària. Entre els idiomes més sol·licitats, destaquen l’àrab, l’urdú, el xinès mandarí, el rus, el francès, el romanès i l’alemany.

Els CAP d’atenció continuada (CUAP), oberts, en la majoria de casos, 24 hores al dia, són l’opció idònia per a problemes de salut urgents de complexitat mitjana i baixa

Altres opcions que poden activar els professionals sempre que calgui són el servei d’atenció psicològica, disponible les 24 hores de tots els dies de l’any, o el de consultes pediàtriques urgents. El 061 Salut Respon disposa, a més, d’una aplicació mòbil pública i gratuïta a la qual poden accedir tant els professionals com la ciutadania. L’app ja es pot actualitzar a la seva darrera versió, la 5.2.0, que entre d’altres millores inclou la possibilitat d’activar videotrucades amb llengua de signes, facilitant així la interacció amb persones sordes. El sistema d’atenció demana els usuaris que s’identifiquen i aportin dades bàsiques com el nom, l’edat, l’adreça o el número de Targeta Sanitària, però el xat de l’aplicació permet fer també consultes anònimes.

Urgències de proximitat

L’altra gran alternativa a les sales d’espera dels hospitals són els CAP d’atenció continuada (CUAP), oberts, en la majoria dels casos, 24 hores al dia, tot i que en alguns punts concrets del territori obren només 12 hores diàries. Aquests centres són l’opció idònia per a problemes de salut urgents de complexitat mitjana i baixa, mentre que els serveis d’urgència hospitalaris donaran prioritat sempre als casos de risc vital, d’alt risc o que exigeixen exploracions múltiples i estabilització fisiològica del pacient.

La majoria dels CUAP disposen d’instal·lacions i instrumental per a fer radiografies i analítiques, fet que garanteix la realització de les exploracions bàsiques necessàries per a obtenir un primer diagnòstic en els casos no tan urgents. És a dir, no només ofereixin una bona alternativa assistencial al pacient, també contribueixen de manera decisiva a la descongestió del serveis d’urgències.

En resum, el protocol d’actuació que recomana el Departament de Salut de la Generalitat quan tenim un problema de salut que pensem que pot ser urgent és, abans de desplaçar-se a un hospital, trucar al 061 o anar al nostre CAP. Aquest ens derivarà, si ho considera necessari, al CUAP més proper. Si el CAP fos tancat, queda l’opció d’acudir directament al Centre d’Urgències d’Atenció Primària. Si tots seguim aquestes senzilles pautes, els serveis d’urgències podran centrar els seus esforços en els casos més greus, evitant així col·lapses puntuals i temps d’espera molt superiors als habituals.

World.title: Amancio Ortega compra por 175 millones un edificio de apartamentos en Londres
World.content:
La valoración de los 15 inmuebles en la capital inglesa supera ya los 4.200 millones

El fundador y primer accionista de Inditex, Amancio Ortega, a través de su brazo inversor Pontegadea, refuerza su presencia en Reino Unido tras adquirir en Londres un complejo de apartamentos por 150 millones de libras (175 millones de euros). De esta forma, Londres se ha convertido en una de las ciudades favoritas de Ortega para invertir, con cerca ya de 15 activos inmobiliarios valorados en conjunto en más de 4.200 millones de euros.

Es la primera adquisición de Ortega en el mercado del residencial para alquiler en Reino Unido, aunque en este segmento ya realizó importantes inversiones en Nueva York, Boston, Chicago o Dublín.

En concreto, el complejo de apartamentos está localizado en el 219 de Baker Street, en pleno barrio londinense de Marylebone, según ha adelantado el medio inmobiliario Green Street News. Esta adquisición se cerró el pasado mes de febrero y ha trascendido ahora al aparecer en el Registro Mercantil británico. Para esta operación la empresa constituyó una nueva filial en el Reino Unido y financió la operación mediante un préstamo intragrupo. El multimillonario español invierte habitualmente en este mercado británico a través de Pontegadea UK o Pontegadea GB.

Reino Unido es uno de los países favoritos de Pontegadea para invertir. Así, su filial británica, Pontegadea UK, cifraba en 2.654,5 millones de libras (unos 3.160 millones de euros) el valor de sus activos inmobiliarios en 2025, un 10,8% más, según las cuentas anuales depositadas en el registro oficial de empresas y sociedades británico.

El valor de las propiedades de inversión de la sociedad a 31 de diciembre de 2025 ascendía a 2.700,3 millones de libras (3.158 millones de euros), un 12,8% más.

Esta nueva compra llega después de que el vehículo inversor de Amancio Ortega desembarcara en Australia de la mano del consorcio liderado por el fondo Macquarie tras completar el pasado viernes la adquisición del ‘holding’ logístico australiano Qube, en una operación valorada en 11.700 millones de dólares australianos (7.165,94 millones de euros).

Además a finales de julio, la firma se reforzó en Francia tras adquirir por 850 millones de euros el complejo de oficinas Capital 8 de París en lo que es la mayor operación inmobiliaria de oficinas individuales ejecutada en la Europa continental desde 2022.

Mientras que a finales de la semana pasada acordó la venta de su participación del 13,7% al Estado portugués en el operador de la red eléctrica Redes Energéticas Nacionais (REN). Una operación que se realizará con la transferencia de 91,7 millones de acciones a la sociedad estatal Parpública.

En Reino Unido, también el pasado año, Ortega adquirió por más de 90 millones de euros un almacén de Amazon en Liverpool, que está alquilada en su totalidad al gigante del comercio electrónico a largo plazo.

Pontegadea ha seguido inviertiendo en 2026 en ladrillo. Además de los citados edificios de Boston y París, en lo que va de ejercicio ha adquirido un edificio de oficinas en Chicago por 440 millones, o sendas naves logísticas operadas por Amazony Lactalis en Canadá por 215 millones.

World.title: El Deportivo regresa con orden y sin mucho talento
World.content:
Ocho años después el Deportivo volvió a Primera División y sumó un punto, un puntiño, que diría Arsenio Iglesias, el referente del club que durante tantos años pregonó la bonanza del orden y el talento. Y ahí, años después de aquellas glorias dirigidas por el recordado entrenador y en tan esperado regreso, anda uno de los nueve campeones de Liga, que trata de ordenarse, pero busca el talento. No siempre lo encuentra. El reinicio entre los grandes lo zanjó con un empate (1-1) ante un buen Elche con el que se presume que competirá por evitar la quema en la clasificación y que le lleva un año de ventaja en la categoría. No es poco bagaje.

DEP Deportivo 1 Leo Román, Ximo Navarro, Bright Ede, Lucas Noubi, Giacomo Quagliata, Bil Nsongo (Zakaria Eddahchouri, min. 59), Lorenzo Amatucci, Jonathan Asp Jensen (Diego Villares, min. 59), Mario Soriano (David Mella, min. 70), Adrià Alti (Luismi Cruz, min. 70) y Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang (Kevin Sánchez, min. 84) ELC Elche 1 Matías Dituro, Víctor Chust, David Affengruber, Germán Valera (Álvaro Padilla, min. 80), Buba Sangaré, Federico Redondo (Tete Morente, min. 59), Gonzalo Villar, Martim Neto (Lucas Cepeda, min. 59), Marc Aguado, Ali Houary (Javier Morcillo, min. 80) y Fer Niño (Umaru, min. 68) Goles 1-0 min. 20: Aubameyang. 1-1 min. 75: Marc Aguado Arbitro Francisco José Hernández Maeso

Tarjetas amarillas Ximo Navarro (min. 25), Lorenzo Amatucci (min. 45), Gonzalo Villar (min. 66), Umaru (min. 87)

El partido tuvo chicha, pero le faltó fútbol y también la animación habitual en Riazor porque el fondo más bullicioso está enfrentado con el club y decidió no animar al equipo, vestido de naranja para hacer visible su protesta. Hubo brega, sudor, intensidad, táctica, pero apenas un par de golpes de magia. Tampoco es cuestión de aguardar alardes entre escuadras llamadas a pelear por la permanencia en la categoría, por más que el Deportivo tenga ansias de reeditar viejas glorias y el Elche venga de una campaña en la que mostró herramientas que animan a intuir una consolidación entre los grandes. No es tan sencillo. En este fútbol picapedrero, Riazor recibió a dos equipos con precauciones, conscientes del daño que les pueden hacer las transiciones y, por tanto, cautos en la circulación de la pelota. Ocurrió lo normal en esas situaciones, el partido se cerró. Lo abrió en una acción episódica Aubameyang porque en este fútbol de detalles siempre, y más que nunca, gobierna el talento. Y el veterano delantero gabonés de trayectoria en Arsenal, Chelsea, Barcelona o Marsella ha llegado a A Coruña con 37 años para explicarle al mundo que sigue vigente quizás no como en sus mejores tiempos, pero al menos al nivel suficiente para marcar diferencias en muchos partidos de una de las mejores ligas del mundo. Lo hizo en una resolución que le retrata como un fuera de serie al bajar del cielo un envío lejano de Amatucci, controlar con el exterior del pie derecho la pelota con algo parecido a un paso de ballet y cruzar con la zurda a la red.

Fue un golazo. Y llegó casi mediada una primera parte en la que el trasteo mantuvo la liza alejada de los porteros. Leo Román, el cancerbero por el que el Deportivo pagó 9 millones de claúsula de rescisión al Mallorca, intervino en el amanecer del partido para detener un intento de Houary. Empezó más vertical el Elche, pero pronto se detuvo. O más bien le frenó el entramado defensivo deportivista. El técnico Antonio Hidalgo ya había anunciado que el balón iba a ser del rival, así que juntó al equipo para esperar su momento. Ofreció escasas fisuras, detalle que es importante para un equipo recién ascendido y más ante un rival que se presume directo. Y cuando hubo alguna grieta ahí estuvo el portero para taparlas casi todas.

Román se hizo gigante para poner una muralla ante la portería local en un doble intento de Fer Niño y Gonzalo Villar cuando el reloj frisaba la hora del partido. El lance avivó a los entrenadores para introducir dos cambios por bando, pero sobre todo a Hidalgo para buscar piernas frescas en la medular. Para ello encontró a su vera a Diego Villares, superviviente del Deportivo que se pasó cuatro años en la tercera categoría del fútbol español, capitán del equipo que en dos cursos en Segunda dio el salto a la élite. Cerca del oropel de estrellas como Aubameyang hay tipos como Villares, que como más de medio Dépor, que hicieron su debut en Primera. Y tocaba correr para guardar la ventaja en el marcador porque el Elche apretó y lo hizo hasta que llegó a un empate que se trabajó durante muchos minutos. Igualó en una desatención local en una de esas traicioneras segundas acciones tras un saque de esquina en la que Marc Aguado, que no es precisamente Fernando Romay, fue lo suficientemente listo como para adelantarse en el primer palos a tirios y troyanos y cabecear a la red.

El Deportivo se revolvió, pero atacó con más entusiasmo que aperos. Le faltó la casi siempre trascendente aportación de Mario Soriano, su faro con balón, que se fue del partido antes de su epílogo después de desgastarse en persecuciones. Le dolió el gol encajado al equipo coruñés, pero tampoco encontró cómo rebelarse ante un Elche que pareció bien trabajado y se fajó para rascar un punto en un final sin colmillo por parte de ambos equipos. Queda mucho por remar para todos.

World.title: Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj
World.content:
Este enclave del Baix Empordà ha logrado conservar la magia de sus playas y calas, goza de algunas de las mejores propuestas culinarias del territorio y atrae por igual a locales y foráneos, permaneciendo en un ventajoso segundo plano a la hora de atraer al turismo masivo

Begur es una localidad catalana cuya fundación los historiadores acostumbran a situar en 1019, con la construcción del castillo de la localidad, aunque sus inicios datan de la época feudal. Ubicada a apenas 30 kilómetros de Girona, esta joya del Baix Empordà consigue permanecer alejada durante gran parte del año de las rutas turísticas masificadas que recorren parajes como Barcelona, la siempre bulliciosa Costa Brava o ciertas zonas del Empordà. Conserva además intacta su capacidad para sorprender al viajero y acumula un buen número de razones que obligan al habitual a seguir volviendo a su calma chicha. En verano la cosa cambia y la población, de apenas 4.000 habitantes, se multiplica por diez, pero, aun así, el pueblo se las ingenia para seguir siendo (relativamente) tranquilo.

Sa Punta, un establecimiento familiar totalmente remodelado de la mano de un grupo de empresarios encabezados por Daniela McLean —ideóloga del proyecto y con amplia experiencia en leyendas de la hostelería de lujo como el Palace Hôtel de Crillon, en París, o el grupo Peninsula Hotels—, se ha convertido en uno de los grandes imanes de esta localidad de cielos limpios y carácter familiar, con su apariencia de casa señorial en cuyo interior se esconde el espíritu de una beach house pensada para apagar el móvil, desenchufar el ordenador y vivir como si el mundo exterior hubiera decidido dejarnos en paz durante unos días.

Más información 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde

El jardín del hotel Sa Punta, en Begur.

Este hotel cuenta con 36 habitaciones, un spa, un restaurante con vocación transversal y sin delirios de grandeza (hay arroces, pero también hamburguesas), una piscina perfecta para los que desean ponerse en remojo en lugar de encaminarse hacia la playa y un entorno donde predomina el verde y una tranquilidad casi desconcertante, teniendo en cuenta los desquiciantes parámetros urbanitas. “Estamos en un lugar emblemático, rodeado de campos, de viñedos y de rutas ideales para darse una vuelta en bici o un buen paseo. Es un hotel muy tranquilo porque hacemos yoga y es solo para adultos. Siempre digo que es un hotel que transmite calma: pensado para desconectar totalmente del estrés. Por eso muchas veces insistimos en lo de la beach house para explicar por qué esto no es un hotel de lujo al uso ni un cuatro estrellas convencional”, explica Sandra Julià, la directora del establecimiento. “Tampoco estamos en primera línea de mar, aunque en cinco minutos puedas plantarte en la playa. Es una zona más elevada, así que tenemos unas vistas preciosas, pero con un ambiente mucho más íntimo”, añade sobre este establecimiento que abre de abril a octubre para adaptarse a las necesidades y deseos de su clientela.

La dificultad de acceder a Begur si uno no dispone de coche (el transporte público funciona en la temporada estival, pero sigue siendo complejo acceder al pueblo) se ha convertido, paradójicamente, en una de las ventajas de la localidad. “Totalmente. Lo cierto es que la gran mayoría de nuestros clientes necesitan coche para llegar hasta aquí y está claro que, si fuera accesible con el tren, el autobús y el transporte público, sería muy diferente. Y no solo para el hotel, para toda la zona. La movilidad aquí ya es complicada. Es cierto que a Begur y a Pals puedes llegar en autobús, pero no llega el tren. Eso hace que sea un destino un poco más exclusivo”, confirma Julià.

Vista del castillo de Begur. BORIS STROUJKO (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Más allá de las virtudes de un alojamiento pensado para el reposo y la desconexión, si uno decide salir de Sa Punta, Begur ofrece una triada insuperable: gastronomía, paseos y un sinfín de destellos del pasado. “Creo que eso es precisamente lo que la gente viene buscando. Pueblos medievales como Pals o Peratallada, lugares históricos, una gastronomía increíble, el arroz de Pals y unas playas preciosas. Todas esas pequeñas calas llenas de encanto”, aporta Julià. Pero a pesar del innegable atractivo de la geografía y la idiosincrasia que recorre cada rincón del Baix Empordà, Julià reconoce que algunos de sus clientes vienen buscando cosas distintas: “Por supuesto, hay de todo y también nos gusta que sea así, tener muchos perfiles distintos y ser capaces de atenderles con la misma solvencia. Hay clientes que vienen únicamente a jugar al golf. Comen aquí todos los días y no quieren hacer nada más. O los ciclistas, que pasan el día entero sobre la bicicleta. ¡Hay de todo!”, sonríe.

Para que no queden dudas, la directora de Sa Punta deja claro que en el hotel se prioriza un enfoque centrado en el adulto. El establecimiento es un gran reclamo para el turista familiar, pero solo con adolescentes, ya que la edad mínima son 12 años. “Por eso tenemos muchas parejas o grupos de amigos que vienen a darse un homenaje culinario, y no hay niños, pero pueden traerse a sus perros… siempre que no pesen más de nueve kilos”, aclara.

El bar exterior del hotel Sa Punta.

Para ponerse las botas

Lo del buen comer es casi una obligación para cualquiera que visite este enclave gerundense. La oferta es amplia, el producto impecable y hay un buen número de lugares que parecen sacados de una de esas películas románticas en las que los protagonistas se ponen las botas con el mar de fondo. AlKostat del Mar (en el hotel Finca Victoria) es uno de esos paraísos: con un coloso como el chef Jordi Vilà, responsable de los fogones de dos templos barceloneses como el Alkimia y Alkostat al mando del establecimiento, esta se ha convertido en una de las citas imprescindibles para los amantes de la buena mesa.

El chef Jordi Vilà está al frente de AlKostat del Mar, en el hotel Finca Victoria.

“AlKostat del Mar es un proyecto que puede adaptarse al territorio y es totalmente permeable a la cocina local. Casi podríamos decir que por sedimentación se acomoda allí donde llega. Creo que hacemos una cocina muy fresca, muy de olores, muy de sabores, sencilla: catalana y tradicional, pero siempre con nuestro toque. Como trabajamos mucho con el producto de temporada, pues hay mucho tomate y mucho pescado a la brasa”, explica Vilà. ¿Un plato imprescindible? “La ensaladilla rusa a la brasa, en la que cada ingrediente pasa por las brasas antes de volver al plato. Creo que explica muy bien lo que hacemos”.

Por supuesto, la competencia es feroz y en la lista de los favoritos de la localidad también sacan la cabeza tótems como Cap Sa Sal y la sidrería Mooma. Si hay ganas de aventura, Far Nomo, en Llafranc, es otra recomendación de primera clase y localidades como Peratallada, Pals y Calella de Palafrugell también ofrecen una gran variedad de mesas en las que ponerse las botas.

Para los amantes de los paseos o las calas, Begur es un seguro de vida: en el camino que lleva de Aiguablava a Platja Fonda puede recorrerse uno de los tramos más bellos del Camí de Ronda de la Costa Brava. El sendero transcurre entre pinos y acantilados, enlazando pequeñas calas y miradores naturales con vistas al Mediterráneo. El recorrido culmina en la mencionada Platja Fonda, una playa de arena oscura encajada entre altas paredes rocosas que sigue conservando una atmósfera casi mágica.

Si uno se queda con ganas de más, nada mejor que apostar por la ruta que lleva desde Cap de Begur a El Semàfor, un recorrido menos conocido que permite adentrarse en una de las zonas más agrestes del litoral de Begur. Un sendero que llega a una antigua estación electro-semafórica (la mencionada, El Semàfor), inaugurada en 1891 para orientar a los barcos de la Costa Brava. En el extremo del Cap de Begur, el edificio se abre hoy como mirador privilegiado sobre el mar.

Con tanto paseo, piscina, bici, golf y banquete, puede que en algún momento apetezca la irremediable tentación del dulce: para eso existe la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, uno de esos sitios a los que hay que ir dispuesto a dejarse aconsejar. “Abrí hace unos seis años y aposté desde el principio por la pastelería tradicional, pero reduciendo un 20% el azúcar. Abro todo el año y, aparte de brazos de gitano, coronas y pasteles como el de requesón (con queso local) o tiramisú con ratafía, mi producto estrella es el buñuelo del Empordà”, cuenta Anna Ferret, que regenta este palacete del dulce en la localidad gerundense.

Uno de los rulos de nata de la la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, en Begur.

La directora de Sa Punta quiere ofrecer a los interesados un último aliciente: “Tenemos un plus, que es algo que a mí me gusta mucho, y es que existe un gran sentimiento de comunidad que a su vez se traduce en una gran dosis de solidaridad: Sa punta forma parte de Costa Brava Centre y yo conozco a la mayoría de los directores de hoteles cercanos. Si tengo un banquete y me faltan sesenta platos, se los pido al hotel de al lado. Siempre nos ayudamos y eso me parece extraordinario en los tiempos que corren”. “Supongo que también es un buen modo de resumir lo que es Begur: un lugar en el que nunca te faltará de nada”, remata Julià.

World.title: Euromillones: comprobar sorteo del martes 18 de agosto
World.content:
El Euromillones es un sorteo que se juega dos veces a la semana, los martes y los viernes.

Comprueba los números premiados en el sorteo de Loterías y Apuestas del Estado de este martes

Comprueba si eres uno de los afortunados con la combinación ganadora del sorteo del Euromillones de este martes 18 de agosto.

El Euromillones es una de las loterías europeas más conocidas y seguidas desde su lanzamiento en 2004, ya que ofrece multitud de premios y se juega en países como España, Francia, Reino Unido, Austria, Bélgica, Irlanda, Luxemburgo, Portugal y Suiza.

El juego de “El Millón”

El sorteo de “El Millón” es la bola extra con la que Euromillones premia a los españoles, ya que únicamente se puede participar desde España. Así, cada martes y viernes se sortea un premio de 1 millón de euros entre todos los boletos de Euromillones que hayan sido vendidos en territorio español.

Para poder ser el ganador de este premio millonario es necesario que el código del boleto coincida con el código de “El Millón” de ese día.
